title.en: Volume 33: Song Yin, Wang Xian, Qu Zun, Zhang Pu, Gu Hun, Gongsun Biao, Zhang Ji, Li Xian, Jia Yi, Xue Ti
title.raw: 卷33 宋隱 王憲 屈遵 張蒲 榖渾 公孫表 張濟 李先 賈彝 薛提 Volume 33: Song Yin, Wang Xian, Qu Zun, Zhang Pu, Gu Hun, Gongsun Biao, Zhang Ji, Li Xian, Jia Yi, Xue Ti

sentences.zh: 宋隱 王憲 屈遵 張蒲 谷渾 公孫表 張濟 李先 賈彝 薛提

translations.literal: Song Yin, Wang Xian, Qu Zun, Zhang Pu, Gu Hun, Gongsun Biao, Zhang Ji, Li Xian, Jia Yi, Xue Ti
translations.idiomatic: Song Yin, Wang Xian, Qu Zun, Zhang Pu, Gu Hun, Gongsun Biao, Zhang Ji, Li Xian, Jia Yi, and Xue Ti

sentences.zh: 宋隱，字處默，西河介休人也。

translations.literal: Song Yin, style name Chumo, was a man of Jiexiu in Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yin, whose style name was Chumo, came from Jiexiu in Xihe commandery.

sentences.zh: 曾祖奭，晉昌黎太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shuo was Jin Governor of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shuo had served as governor of Changli under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 後為慕容廆長史。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Clerk to Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: He later became chief clerk to Murong Hui.

sentences.zh: 祖活，中書監。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huo was Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huo held the post of Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父恭，尚書、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Gong was Minister of Works and Governor of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gong served as Minister of Works and as governor of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 慕容儁徙鄴，恭始家於廣平列人焉。

translations.literal: When Murong Jun moved to Ye, Gong first established his household at Lieren in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Jun moved the capital to Ye, Gong first settled the family at Lieren in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 隱性至孝，年十三，便有成人之志，專精好學，不以兵難易操。

translations.literal: Yin was by nature extremely filial; at age thirteen he already had the ambition of a grown man, devoted himself to concentrated study, and did not let warfare alter his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was by nature deeply filial; at thirteen he already showed the resolve of a mature man, threw himself into study, and did not let the turmoil of war change his ways.

sentences.zh: 仕慕容垂，歷尚書郎、太子中舍人、本州別駕。

translations.literal: He served Murong Chui, successively as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and Aide-de-Camp of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the service of Murong Chui and rose through the posts of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Attendant of the Heir Apparent, and provincial aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 太祖平中山，拜隱尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: When the Taizu pacified Zhongshan, Yin was appointed Director of the Personnel Section of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu pacified Zhongshan, Yin was appointed director of the personnel section in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 車駕還北，詔隱以本官輔衞王儀鎮中山。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned north, an edict ordered Yin, in his existing office, to assist Prince Wei Yi in garrisoning Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned north, he ordered Yin to keep his present title and assist Prince Wei Yi in holding Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 尋轉行臺右丞，領選如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Mobile Secretariat, still overseeing selection as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Right Vice Director of the Mobile Secretariat while continuing to oversee personnel selection as before.

sentences.zh: 屢以老病乞骸骨，太祖不許。

translations.literal: He repeatedly begged to retire on grounds of age and illness, but the Taizu would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked several times to retire because of age and illness, but the Taizu refused.

sentences.zh: 尋以母喪歸列人。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he returned to Lieren for his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went home to Lieren to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 既葬，被徵，固辭以病，而州郡切以期會，隱乃棄妻子，間行避焉。

translations.literal: After the burial he was summoned; he firmly declined on grounds of illness, but the province and commandery pressed him with deadlines, so Yin abandoned wife and children and slipped away by secret paths to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Once the burial was over he was recalled, but he firmly pleaded illness; when the province and commandery pressed him to appear on schedule, he left wife and children behind and fled by back roads to escape service.

sentences.zh: 後匿於長樂之經縣，數年而卒。

translations.literal: Later he hid in Jing County in Changle and died after several years.
translations.idiomatic: He later hid in Jing County in Changle, where he died after several years.

sentences.zh: 臨終謂其子姪等曰：「苟能入順父兄，出悌鄉黨，仕郡幸而至功曹史，以忠清奉之，則足矣，不勞遠詣臺閣。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he told his sons and nephews: "If you can be obedient to father and elder brothers at home and deferential to the community abroad, and if in office in the commandery you are fortunate enough to reach the post of Merit Officer, serving with loyalty and integrity—that is enough; there is no need to travel far to the central offices.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he told his sons and nephews: "If at home you obey your fathers and elder brothers and abroad you are dutiful to your neighbors, and if in commandery service you are lucky enough to become a merit officer and serve with loyalty and integrity, that is enough. Do not trouble yourselves to seek posts far away at court.

sentences.zh: 恐汝不能富貴，而徒延門戶之累耳。

translations.literal: I fear you will not attain wealth and honor, and will only prolong the burdens on our house."
translations.idiomatic: I fear you will never win wealth and rank, and will only bring further trouble on our clan."

sentences.zh: 若忘吾言，是為無若父也，使鬼而有知，吾不歸食矣。

translations.literal: If you forget my words, you will be as though you had no father; if ghosts have awareness, I shall not return to receive offerings."
translations.idiomatic: If you forget what I say, you will be sons without a father; and if the dead have knowledge, I shall not come back to accept your offerings."

sentences.zh: 」有五子。

translations.literal: He had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons.

sentences.zh: 第三子溫，世祖時徵拜中書博士。

translations.literal: His third son Wen, in the time of the Shizu, was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Wen was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Secretariat in the reign of Emperor Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 卒，追贈建威將軍、豫州刺史，列人定侯。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Establishes Might and Governor of Yuzhou, and enfeoffed as Marquis Ding of Lieren.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made General Who Establishes Might and governor of Yuzhou, with the title Marquis Ding of Lieren.

sentences.zh: 溫弟演，顯祖初從征彭城有功，拜明威將軍、濟北太守。

translations.literal: Wen's younger brother Yan, at the beginning of the Xianzu's reign, followed the campaign against Pengcheng with merit and was appointed General of Illustrious Might and Governor of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: Wen's younger brother Yan distinguished himself in the early campaigns against Pengcheng under Emperor Xiaowen and was made General of Illustrious Might and governor of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 演子鮒，字伯魚。

translations.literal: Yan's son Fu, style name Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Fu, whose style name was Boyu,

sentences.zh: 州別駕。

translations.literal: was Aide-de-Camp of the province.
translations.idiomatic: served as provincial aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 隱弟輔，字處仁。

translations.literal: Yin's younger brother Fu, style name Churen.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's younger brother Fu, whose style name was Churen,

sentences.zh: 少慷慨有大操，博覽羣書。

translations.literal: From youth was generous and high-minded, with great moral resolve, and read widely among the classics.
translations.idiomatic: was from youth generous and high-minded, with a strong sense of principle, and read widely.

sentences.zh: 州辟別駕。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as Aide-de-Camp.
translations.idiomatic: The province recruited him as aide-de-camp.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 隱叔父洽，為慕容垂尚書。

translations.literal: Yin's uncle Qia served Murong Chui as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's uncle Qia was a minister of works under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 太祖之圍中山也，洽率所領專守北圍。

translations.literal: When the Taizu besieged Zhongshan, Qia led his forces in holding the northern encirclement alone.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taizu's siege of Zhongshan, Qia commanded his troops in defending the northern sector of the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 當洽所統，官軍多被傷殺，太祖特深忿恨。

translations.literal: In the sector Qia commanded, many of the imperial troops were wounded and killed, and the Taizu harbored a special deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In the sector under Qia's command many imperial soldiers were killed or wounded, and the Taizu came to hate him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 及城平，遂殺之。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he was put to death.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Qia was executed.

sentences.zh: 子順、訓並下腐刑。

translations.literal: His sons Shun and Xun were both subjected to castration.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Shun and Xun were both sentenced to castration.

sentences.zh: 洽第四子宣，字道茂，時年數歲，親人竊逃以免。

translations.literal: Qia's fourth son Xuan, style name Daomao, was only a few years old; kinsmen secretly fled with him to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Qia's fourth son Xuan, whose style name was Daomao, was only a few years old when relatives smuggled him away to safety.

sentences.zh: 後與范陽盧玄、勃海高允及從子愔俱被徵，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: Later, together with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, and his cousin Yin, he was summoned and appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned together with Lu Xuan of Fanyang, Gao Yun of Bohai, and his cousin Yin, and appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋兼散騎常侍，使劉義隆。

translations.literal: Soon he was also made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and sent as envoy to Liu Yilong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon added the post of Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and was sent on embassy to Liu Yilong of Song.

sentences.zh: 加冠軍將軍，賜爵中都侯，領中書侍郎，行司隸校尉。

translations.literal: He was given the additional title General Who Establishes the Army, enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongdu, made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and acted as Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Establishes the Army, enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhongdu, made supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and commissioned as acting Colonel Director of Retainers.

sentences.zh: 真君七年卒，贈司隸，諡簡侯。

translations.literal: He died in the seventh year of Zhenjun; posthumously granted Colonel Director of Retainers, with the posthumous title Marquis Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year of the Zhenjun era and was posthumously made Colonel Director of Retainers, with the posthumous title Marquis Jian.

sentences.zh: 子謨，字乾仁，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Mo, style name Qianren, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mo, whose style name was Qianren, inherited the marquisate.

sentences.zh: 卒於遼西太守。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Governor of Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office as governor of Liaoxi.

sentences.zh: 子鸞，字珍和，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Luan, style name Zhenhe, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Luan, whose style name was Zhenhe, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 東莞太守。

translations.literal: He was Governor of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 鸞弟瓊，字普賢。

translations.literal: Luan's younger brother Qiong, style name Puxian.
translations.idiomatic: Luan's younger brother Qiong, whose style name was Puxian,

sentences.zh: 少以孝行稱，母曾病，季秋之月，思瓜不已。

translations.literal: was famed from youth for filial conduct; when his mother once fell ill, in the late autumn month she longed endlessly for melons.
translations.idiomatic: was known from youth for filial devotion; when his mother fell ill one late autumn, she could not stop thinking of melons.

sentences.zh: 瓊夢想見之，求而遂獲，時人稱異。

translations.literal: Qiong dreamed he saw them, sought them and obtained them; people of the time called it extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong dreamed of melons, searched for them, and found them; people at the time regarded it as a marvel.

sentences.zh: 母終，州郡屢辟，皆不就。

translations.literal: After his mother's death the province and commandery repeatedly recruited him, but he never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death the province and commandery summoned him repeatedly, but he never took office.

sentences.zh: 卒於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子仲美，武定末，尚書水部郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhongmei, at the end of the Wuding era, was Gentleman of the Water Section in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongmei, late in the Wuding era, served as Gentleman of the Water Section in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 子崇，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 子仲智襲。

translations.literal: His son Zhongzhi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongzhi inherited in turn.

sentences.zh: 歷中書侍郎、安西將軍、幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as supervisor of the Masters of Writing, General Who Pacifies the West, and governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 有清平之稱。

translations.literal: He had the reputation of being upright and fair.
translations.idiomatic: He won a reputation for integrity and fair dealing.

sentences.zh: 崇弟嶷，字道長。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Ni, style name Daochang.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brother Ni, whose style name was Daochang,

sentences.zh: 少以父任為中書學生，稍遷南部大夫。

translations.literal: From youth, through his father's position, he became a student of the Secretariat; he was gradually promoted to Grandee of the Southern Section.
translations.idiomatic: entered the Secretariat school through his father's office and was gradually promoted to Grandee of the Southern Section.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，出使巡察青、徐、兗、豫，撫慰新附，觀省風俗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Gaozu's reign he was sent out to inspect Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu, to comfort the newly submitted and observe local customs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was sent to inspect Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu, to reassure the newly submitted populations and observe local customs.

sentences.zh: 還，遷南部尚書，在任十四年。

translations.literal: On his return he was transferred to Minister of the Southern Section and held office fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Minister of the Southern Section and held the post for fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 時南州多事，文奏盈几，訟者填門。

translations.literal: At that time the southern provinces were full of troubles; documents piled on his desk and litigants filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The southern provinces were then in constant turmoil; documents piled on his desk and litigants crowded his gate.

sentences.zh: 嶷性儒緩，委隨不斷，終日在坐，昏睡而已。

translations.literal: Ni was by nature mild and slow, lax and indecisive; he spent whole days at his seat doing nothing but drowsing.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was mild and unhurried by nature, lax and unable to decide; he spent whole days at his desk doing nothing but dozing.

sentences.zh: 李訢、鄧宗慶等號為明察，勤理時務，而二人終見誅戮，餘十數人或黜或免，唯嶷卒得自保。

translations.literal: Li Xin, Deng Zongqing, and others were famed for sharp discernment and diligent handling of affairs, yet those two in the end were executed; of the remaining dozen or so, some were dismissed and some removed—only Ni in the end preserved himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xin, Deng Zongqing, and others were known for sharp judgment and tireless attention to business, yet both men were eventually executed; of more than a dozen others some were dismissed and some removed from office—only Ni survived to the end.

sentences.zh: 時人為之語曰：「實癡實昏，終得保存。

translations.literal: People of the time made a saying about him: "Truly stupid, truly muddled—yet in the end he kept himself safe."
translations.idiomatic: People of the day said of him: "Genuinely dull, genuinely befuddled—and yet he kept himself safe in the end."

sentences.zh: 」加散騎常侍、右將軍，賜爵東平侯。

translations.literal: He was given the additional posts of Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and General of the Right, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and General of the Right, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜安東將軍，進爵樂安公。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and advanced to Duke of Lean.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and raised to Duke of Lean.

sentences.zh: 出為持節、鎮西將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Qinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out bearing the staff of authority as General Who Pacifies the West and governor of Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 改為華山公，散騎常侍如故。

translations.literal: His title was changed to Duke of Huashan, while his post as Regular Attendant of the Cavalry remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Duke of Huashan while he retained the post of Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 後入為內都大官。

translations.literal: Later he entered the capital as Grand Officer of the Inner Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned to court as Grand Officer of the Inner Capital.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子祖念，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zunian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zunian inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 官至東平太守。

translations.literal: He reached the post of Governor of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of governor of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 例降爵為侯。

translations.literal: By regulation his noble rank was reduced to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Under the usual rule his ducal title was reduced to a marquisate.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈寧朔將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子慶鍾，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Qingzhong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qingzhong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 給事中。

translations.literal: He was Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Attendant Within the Yellow Gates.

sentences.zh: 貪穢無行，坐事爵除。

translations.literal: Greedy and corrupt, without proper conduct, he lost his title for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt and without principle, he was stripped of his title for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 祖念弟雲，字羅漢，頗有風尚。

translations.literal: Zunian's younger brother Yun, style name Luohan, had considerable moral distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Zunian's younger brother Yun, whose style name was Luohan, had real moral distinction.

sentences.zh: 自尚書郎入為中書舍人。

translations.literal: From Gentleman of the Masters of Writing he entered the court as Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from the post of Gentleman of the Masters of Writing into the court as Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 轉司州別駕、光祿少卿，改授衞尉少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Aide-de-Camp of Sizhou and Vice Director of the Household Revenue, then reassigned as Vice Director of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to aide-de-camp of Sizhou and Vice Director of the Household Revenue, then reassigned as Vice Director of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 出為冠軍將軍、尚書、兗州刺史，尋進號征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes the Army, Minister of Works, and Governor of Yanzhou; soon his title was advanced to General Who Captures the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General Who Establishes the Army, minister of works, and governor of Yanzhou, and soon promoted to General Who Captures the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 在州坐受所部荊山戍主杜虞財貨，又取官絹，因染割易，御史糾劾，付廷尉。

translations.literal: While in the province he was convicted of accepting goods from Du Yu, commander of the Jingshan garrison under his authority, and also of taking official silk, altering it by dyeing and cutting for exchange; the censor impeached him and he was handed to the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In office he accepted valuables from Du Yu, commander of the Jingshan garrison under his command, and also took official silk cloth, which he altered by dyeing and cutting for private trade; the censor impeached him and he was handed over to the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 遇赦免。

translations.literal: He encountered an amnesty and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned in a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 熙平二年卒官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiping he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the second year of the Xiping era.

sentences.zh: 贈平南將軍、豫州刺史，諡曰文昭。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Yuzhou, with the posthumous epithet Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the South and governor of Yuzhou, with the posthumous epithet Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 有九子。

translations.literal: He had nine sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had nine sons.

sentences.zh: 長子昕，字元景。

translations.literal: His eldest son Xin, style name Yuanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Xin, whose style name was Yuanjing,

sentences.zh: 武定末，太子詹事。

translations.literal: at the end of the Wuding era was Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: late in the Wuding era served as Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 昕弟暉，字元旭。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brother Hui, style name Yuanxu.
translations.idiomatic: Xin's younger brother Hui, whose style name was Yuanxu,

sentences.zh: 早稱機悟。

translations.literal: was early famed for quick wit.
translations.idiomatic: was praised early on for quick intelligence.

sentences.zh: 歷尚書儀曹郎、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Gentleman of the Ceremonial Section in the Ministry of Works and Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Gentleman of the Ceremonial Section in the Ministry of Works and as Attendant of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、鎮軍將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the Army, and Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the Army, and governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 暉弟旰，字仲明。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Gan, style name Zhongming.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Gan, whose style name was Zhongming,

sentences.zh: 祕書郎、司徒主簿。

translations.literal: was Secretary and Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: served as secretary and chief clerk to the Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 天平中，為盜所害。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 屈遵，字子皮，[2]昌黎徒河人也。

translations.literal: Qu Zun, style name Zipi, [2] was a man of Tuhe in Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Zun, whose style name was Zipi, [2] came from Tuhe in Changli commandery.

sentences.zh: 博學多藝，名著當時。

translations.literal: Learned and skilled in many arts, his fame was outstanding in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and accomplished in many fields, he was celebrated in his day.

sentences.zh: 為慕容永尚書僕射，武垣公。

translations.literal: He served Murong Yong as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and as Duke of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Yong as vice director of the Masters of Writing and as Duke of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 永滅，垂以為博陵令。

translations.literal: When Yong was destroyed, Chui made him Magistrate of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: After Yong's fall, Chui appointed him magistrate of Boling.

sentences.zh: 太祖南伐，車駕幸魯口，博陵太守申永南奔河外，高陽太守崔玄伯東走海濱，屬城長吏率多逃竄。

translations.literal: When the Taizu campaigned south, the imperial carriage reached Lukou; the Governor of Boling Shen Yong fled south beyond the river, the Governor of Gaoyang Cui Xuanbo fled east to the seacoast, and the chief officials of subordinate counties for the most part scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taizu's southern campaign the emperor reached Lukou; the governor of Boling, Shen Yong, fled south beyond the Yellow River, the governor of Gaoyang, Cui Xuanbo, fled east toward the coast, and most of the county magistrates under them ran away.

sentences.zh: 遵獨告其吏民曰：「往年寶師大敗，今茲垂征不還，天之棄燕，人弗支也。

translations.literal: Zun alone told his officials and people: "In former years Prince Bao's army was utterly defeated; now Chui has gone on campaign and will not return—Heaven has abandoned Yan, and men cannot sustain it.
translations.idiomatic: Zun alone addressed his officials and people: "In past years Prince Bao's army was crushed; now Chui has marched out and will not come back. Heaven has abandoned Yan, and men cannot hold it up.

sentences.zh: 魏帝神武命世，寬仁善納，御眾百萬，號令若一，此湯武之師。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor is divinely martial and destined for his age, broad and benevolent and skilled at accepting men; he commands a host of a million, his orders unified as one—this is an army of Tang and Wu."
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor is divinely martial and born for his age, magnanimous and skilled at winning men over; he commands a million troops and his orders run as one. This is an army in the mold of Tang and Wu."

sentences.zh: 吾欲歸命，爾等勉之，勿遇嘉運而為禍先。

translations.literal: I wish to submit to their command; you all exert yourselves, and do not, when you meet a fine fortune, become the first to bring disaster.
translations.idiomatic: I mean to surrender to them; do your best, and do not let a turn of good fortune make you the first to bring ruin upon yourselves.

sentences.zh: 」遂歸太祖。

translations.literal: Then he submitted to the Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: With that he surrendered to the Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖素聞其名，厚加禮焉。

translations.literal: The Taizu had long heard his name and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu had long known his reputation and received him with exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 拜中書令，出納王言，兼總文誥。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat, issuing and receiving the king's words, and also overseeing all written edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Secretariat, charged with conveying the sovereign's words and overseeing all written proclamations.

sentences.zh: 中原既平，賜爵下蔡子。

translations.literal: When the Central Plains were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xiaxia.
translations.idiomatic: After the Central Plains were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Xiaxia.

sentences.zh: 從駕還京師，卒，時年七十。

translations.literal: He followed the imperial carriage back to the capital and died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor back to the capital and died there at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子須，襲。

translations.literal: His son Xu inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 除長樂太守，加鎮遠將軍，進爵信都侯。

translations.literal: He was appointed Governor of Changle, given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant, and advanced to Marquis of Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed governor of Changle, made General Who Pacifies the Distant, and raised to Marquis of Xindu.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈寧北將軍、昌黎公，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the North and Duke of Changli, with the posthumous epithet Gong.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Duke of Changli, with the posthumous epithet Gong.

sentences.zh: 少子處珍，襲爵。

translations.literal: His youngest son Chuzhen inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Chuzhen inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 處珍卒，子車渠襲爵。

translations.literal: When Chuzhen died, his son Chequ inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuzhen died, his son Chequ inherited in turn.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，出為東陽鎮將。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Gaozu's reign he went out as Garrison General of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was sent out as garrison general of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈青州刺史，諡曰莊。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Governor of Qingzhou, with the posthumous epithet Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made governor of Qingzhou, with the posthumous epithet Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 長子觀，早卒。

translations.literal: His eldest son Guan died young.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Guan died young.

sentences.zh: 世祖愍之，賜其子男爵。

translations.literal: The Shizu pitied him and granted his son a baron's title.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu took pity on him and granted his son a baron's title.

sentences.zh: 觀弟道賜，襲祖爵。

translations.literal: Guan's younger brother Daoci inherited their grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: Guan's younger brother Daoci inherited their grandfather's title.

sentences.zh: [4]道賜，少以父任，內侍左右。

translations.literal: [4] Daoci, from youth through his father's position, attended within as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Daoci entered court service through his father's office while still young and attended at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 稍遷主客，進為尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Director of Guests, advanced to Minister of Works, and given the additional post of Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Director of Guests, then to Minister of Works, with the added title of Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，機辯有辭氣，世祖甚器之。

translations.literal: Skilled in horsemanship and archery, quick-witted and forceful in speech, he was greatly valued by the Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in riding and archery, quick-witted and forceful in debate, he won great favor from Emperor Taiwu.

sentences.zh: 從征蓋吳，遷尚書右僕射，加侍中。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Gai Wu and was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, with the additional post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the campaign against Gai Wu and was made Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing with the added title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 還至雁門，暴疾卒。

translations.literal: On the return, when they reached Yanmen, he died suddenly of illness.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home he reached Yanmen and died suddenly of illness.

sentences.zh: 諡曰哀公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Ai.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Duke Ai.

sentences.zh: 子拔，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Ba inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ba inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 拔少好陰陽學。

translations.literal: Ba from youth loved the study of yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ba was drawn to the study of yin-yang cosmology.

sentences.zh: 世祖追思其父祖，年十四，以為南部大夫。

translations.literal: The Shizu, recalling his father and grandfather, at age fourteen appointed him Grandee of the Southern Section.
translations.idiomatic: In memory of his father and grandfather, the emperor appointed him Grandee of the Southern Section at the age of fourteen.

sentences.zh: 時世祖南伐，擒劉義隆將胡盛之，以付拔。

translations.literal: At that time the Shizu campaigned south and captured Liu Yilong's general Hu Shengzhi, entrusting him to Ba.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern campaign the emperor captured Hu Shengzhi, a general of Liu Yilong, and placed him in Ba's custody.

sentences.zh: 拔酒醉，不覺盛之逃去。

translations.literal: Ba was drunk and did not notice Shengzhi's escape.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was drunk and did not notice when Shengzhi escaped.

sentences.zh: 世祖大怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: The Shizu was furious and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 將伏鑕，世祖愴然曰：「若鬼而有知，長生問其子孫，朕何以應之？

translations.literal: As he was about to be executed, the Shizu said sorrowfully: "If ghosts have awareness and Changsheng asks his descendants, how shall I answer him?"
translations.idiomatic: As the execution was about to take place, the emperor said in distress: "If the dead have knowledge and Changsheng asks his descendants what became of them, what answer can I give?"

sentences.zh: 」乃赦拔，免為散大夫。

translations.literal: He then pardoned Ba and demoted him to Grandee Without Portfolio.
translations.idiomatic: He then pardoned Ba and reduced him to the rank of Grandee Without Portfolio.

sentences.zh: 後顯祖以其功臣子，拜營州刺史。

translations.literal: Later the Xianzu, because he was the son of a meritorious minister, appointed him Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xiaowen, treating him as the son of a meritorious minister, appointed him governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，子永興襲爵。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Yongxing inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his son Yongxing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 張蒲，字玄則，河內脩武人，本名謨，後改為蒲。

translations.literal: Zhang Pu, style name Xuanze, was a man of Xiuwu in Henei; his original name was Mo, later changed to Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu, whose style name was Xuanze, came from Xiuwu in Henei commandery; his original given name was Mo, which he later changed to Pu.

sentences.zh: 漢太尉延之後。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Yan, Grand Commandant under Han.
translations.idiomatic: He traced his descent to Zhang Yan, Grand Commandant under the Han.

sentences.zh: 父攀，慕容垂御史中丞、兵部尚書，以清方稱。

translations.literal: His father Pan was Censor-in-Chief and Minister of War under Murong Chui, famed for integrity and rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pan had served Murong Chui as censor-in-chief and minister of war and was known for integrity and rectitude.

sentences.zh: 蒲少有父風，頗涉文史，以端謹見知，為慕容寶陽平、河間二郡太守，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Pu from youth had his father's manner, was fairly versed in literature and history, and was known for propriety and caution; he served Murong Bao as Governor of the two commanderies Yangping and Hejian, and as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Pu showed his father's character from youth, had some grounding in letters and history, and won notice for propriety and discretion; he served Murong Bao as governor of Yangping and Hejian and as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 太祖定中山，寶之官司敍用者，多降品秩。

translations.literal: When the Taizu pacified Zhongshan, most of Bao's officials who were retained had their ranks reduced.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu pacified Zhongshan, most of Bao's officials who were kept in service had their ranks reduced.

sentences.zh: 既素聞蒲名，仍拜為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Having long heard Pu's name, he still appointed him Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu had long known Pu's reputation and nevertheless appointed him Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 天興中，以蒲清謹方正，遷東部大人。

translations.literal: In the Tianxing era, because Pu was pure, cautious, and upright, he was transferred to Grandee of the Eastern Section.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxing era he was transferred to Grandee of the Eastern Section on account of his purity, caution, and rectitude.

sentences.zh: 後拜太中大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，為內都大官，賜爵泰昌子，參決庶獄，私謁不行，號為公正。

translations.literal: When the Taizong took the throne, he became Grand Officer of the Inner Capital, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Taichang, participated in deciding ordinary cases, would not accept private petitions, and was called "the fair one."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, Pu became Grand Officer of the Inner Capital, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Taichang, helped decide ordinary legal cases, refused private petitions, and was known as "the fair judge."

sentences.zh: 泰常初，丁零翟猛雀驅逼吏民入白𡼏山，謀為大逆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang, the Dingling Zhai Mengque drove officials and people into Baizhong Mountain, plotting great rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taichang era the Dingling leader Zhai Mengque forced officials and commoners into Baizhong Mountain in a plot of outright rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔蒲與冀州刺史長孫道生等往討。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Pu, together with Changsun Daosheng, Governor of Jizhou, and others to go suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Pu, together with Changsun Daosheng, governor of Jizhou, and others to go and suppress the revolt.

sentences.zh: 道生等欲徑以大兵擊之，蒲曰：「良民所以從猛雀者，非樂亂而為，皆逼凶威，強服之耳。

translations.literal: Daosheng and others wished to attack them directly with a large force; Pu said: "The reason good people follow Mengque is not that they delight in disorder; all are compelled by fierce intimidation and forced to submit—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng and the others wanted to strike at once with a large army. Pu said: "The reason ordinary people follow Mengque is not that they love rebellion; they are all driven by brutal intimidation and forced to submit.

sentences.zh: 今若直以大軍臨之，吏民雖欲返善，其道無由。

translations.literal: If we now bring a great army directly against them, though officials and people may wish to return to goodness, they will have no way to do so.
translations.idiomatic: If we march a great army straight against them now, even when officials and people wish to return to loyalty they will have no way to do so.

sentences.zh: 又懼誅夷，必并勢而距官軍，然後入山恃阻，誑惑愚民。

translations.literal: Moreover, fearing extermination, they will surely combine their strength to resist the imperial army, then enter the mountains relying on difficult terrain and deceive the foolish populace.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing massacre, they will surely unite to resist the imperial army, then retreat into the mountains and use the terrain to deceive the common people.

sentences.zh: 其變未易圖也。

translations.literal: Such a turn of events would not be easy to deal with."
translations.idiomatic: Such a turn of events would not be easy to overcome."

sentences.zh: 不如先遣使喻之，使民不與猛雀同謀者無坐，則民必喜而俱降矣。

translations.literal: It would be better first to send envoys to instruct them, declaring that people who did not conspire with Mengque would not be punished—then the people will surely rejoice and all submit.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to send envoys first and announce that those who did not join Mengque's plot would not be punished; then the people will surely rejoice and surrender together.

sentences.zh: 」道生甚以為然，具以奏聞。

translations.literal: Daosheng greatly approved and reported it all to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng strongly agreed and reported the plan in full to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔蒲軍前慰喻。

translations.literal: The Taizong ordered Pu to go before the army and offer reassurance and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan ordered Pu to go ahead of the army and offer reassurance and instruction.

sentences.zh: 乃下數千家，還其本屬，蒲皆安集之。

translations.literal: Several thousand households then came down the mountain and were returned to their original jurisdictions; Pu settled them all in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand households then came down from the mountains and were returned to their home districts; Pu settled them all peacefully.

sentences.zh: 猛雀與親黨百餘人奔逃。

translations.literal: Mengque and more than a hundred close followers fled.
translations.idiomatic: Mengque fled with more than a hundred close followers.

sentences.zh: 蒲與道生等追斬猛雀首，送京師。

translations.literal: Pu and Daosheng pursued him, beheaded Mengque, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Pu and Daosheng pursued him, cut off Mengque's head, and sent it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 後劉裕寇竊河表，以蒲為南中郎將、南蠻校尉，隸平南大將軍長孫嵩往禦之。

translations.literal: Later, when Liu Yu raided and seized the lands south of the river, Pu was made General of the Southern Gentlemen, Colonel of the Southern Barbarians, and placed under the Pacifier of the South, Grand General Changsun Song, to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Liu Yu invaded the territory south of the Yellow River, Pu was made General of the Southern Gentlemen and Colonel of the Southern Barbarians and placed under Grand General Changsun Song, Pacifier of the South, to resist him.

sentences.zh: 裕入長安，乃還。

translations.literal: When Yu entered Chang'an, they returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu entered Chang'an, the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後改為壽張子，與安平公叔孫建將兵自平原東渡，[5]徇下劉義符青兗諸郡。

translations.literal: Later his title was changed to Viscount of Shouzhang; together with the Duke of Ping'an, Shusun Jian, he led troops crossing east from Pingyuan [5] and subjugated the Qing and Yan commanderies of Liu Yifu.
translations.idiomatic: His title was later changed to Viscount of Shouzhang; together with Duke of Ping'an Shusun Jian he led troops across the plain from Pingyuan [5] and brought under control the Qing and Yan commanderies held by Liu Yifu.

sentences.zh: 詔加陳兵將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict added the titles General Who Displays Troops and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made General Who Displays Troops and governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 又與建攻青州，不克而還。

translations.literal: Again with Jian he attacked Qingzhou but could not take it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Jian in an attack on Qingzhou, failed to take it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，以蒲清貧，妻子衣食不給，乃出為相州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Shizu took the throne, because Pu was poor and upright and his wife and children lacked food and clothing, he was sent out as Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu took the throne, seeing that Pu was upright but so poor that his wife and children lacked adequate food and clothing, the court sent him out as governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 扶弱抑強，進善黜惡，教化大行。

translations.literal: He supported the weak and restrained the strong, promoted the good and removed the wicked, and moral instruction flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He supported the weak and restrained the strong, promoted the good and removed the wicked, and moral instruction flourished throughout the province.

sentences.zh: 始光三年卒於州，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shiguang he died in the province, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the third year of the Shiguang era, at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 吏民痛惜之。

translations.literal: Officials and people grieved deeply for him.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and commoners mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 蒲在謀臣之列，屢出為將，朝廷清論，常為稱首。

translations.literal: Pu stood among the strategists, was repeatedly sent out as a general, and in the court's sober discussions was often ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Pu ranked among the emperor's chief advisers, was repeatedly sent out as a general, and in the court's sober discussions was often placed first.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、廣平公，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Guangping, with the posthumous epithet Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and Duke of Guangping, with the posthumous epithet Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子昭，有志操。

translations.literal: His son Zhao had moral resolve.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhao had strong moral character.

sentences.zh: 天興中，以功臣子為太學生。

translations.literal: In the Tianxing era, as the son of a meritorious minister he became a student of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianxing era he entered the Imperial Academy as the son of a meritorious minister.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，為內主書。

translations.literal: When the Taizong took the throne, he became Chief Secretary Within.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne, he became chief secretary within the palace.

sentences.zh: 後襲父爵。

translations.literal: Later he inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: He later inherited his father's title.

sentences.zh: 神䴥中，從征蠕蠕，以功進爵脩武侯，加平遠將軍。

translations.literal: In the Shenju era he followed the campaign against the Rouran and, for merit, was advanced to Marquis of Xiuwu and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenju era he joined the campaign against the Rouran and, for his merit, was raised to Marquis of Xiuwu and made General Who Pacifies the Distant.

sentences.zh: 延和二年，出為幽州刺史，開府，加寧東將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanhe he went out as Governor of Youzhou, opened a headquarters, and was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yanhe era he was sent out as governor of Youzhou with his own headquarters and the added title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 時幽州年穀不登，州廩虛罄，民多菜色。

translations.literal: At that time Youzhou's harvest failed, the provincial granaries were empty, and many of the people showed the pallor of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou had suffered crop failure that year; the provincial granaries were empty and many people showed the pallor of hunger.

sentences.zh: 昭謂民吏曰：「何我之不德而遇其時乎？

translations.literal: Zhao said to the officials and people: "How is it that my lack of virtue has met with such a time?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao said to officials and people alike: "What lack of virtue in me has brought on such a time?"

sentences.zh: 」乃使富人通濟貧乏，車馬之家糴運外境，貧弱者勸以農桑。

translations.literal: He then had the wealthy extend relief to the poor; households with carts and horses bought grain from outside the region and transported it in, while the poor and weak were urged to devote themselves to farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: He then had the wealthy extend relief to the poor, households with transport buy grain from outside the region, and the poorest urged to devote themselves to farming and sericulture.

sentences.zh: 歲乃大熟。

translations.literal: That year the harvest was abundant.
translations.idiomatic: That year brought a great harvest.

sentences.zh: 士女稱頌之。

translations.literal: Men and women praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Men and women throughout the province praised him.

sentences.zh: 在任三年，卒。

translations.literal: After three years in office he died.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office he died.

sentences.zh: 子昶，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chang inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 早卒。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 昶弟靈符。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Lingfu.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Lingfu

sentences.zh: 真君八年，補中書博士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenjun he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat in the eighth year of the Zhenjun era.

sentences.zh: 和平中，咸陽郡民趙昌聚黨作逆，百姓騷動。

translations.literal: In the Heping era the people of Xianyang commandery, Zhao Chang, gathered a faction and rebelled, and the common people were thrown into turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: During the Heping era Zhao Chang of Xianyang commandery gathered a faction and rebelled, throwing the populace into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 詔靈符宣旨慰喻，民乃復業。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Lingfu to proclaim the imperial will and offer reassurance; the people then returned to their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Lingfu to proclaim the imperial will and reassure the people, and they then returned to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 天安初，遷中書侍郎，賜爵昌國子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an he was transferred to Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Viscount of Changguo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tian'an era he was made Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and enfeoffed as Viscount of Changguo.

sentences.zh: 延興中，使南豫州，觀察風俗。

translations.literal: In the Yanxing era he was sent to Southern Yuzhou to observe local customs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanxing era he was sent to Southern Yuzhou to observe local customs.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，除建威將軍、廣平太守。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was appointed General Who Establishes Might and Governor of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Taihe era he was made General Who Establishes Might and governor of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 還為尚書左丞，司州大中正。

translations.literal: On his return he became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Chief Rectifier of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Chief Rectifier of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 後除鎮遠將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distant and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made General Who Pacifies the Distant and governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 十六年，轉光州刺史，加立忠將軍。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Governor of Guangzhou and given the additional title General Who Establishes Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to governor of Guangzhou with the added title General Who Establishes Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 谷渾，字元沖，昌黎人也。

translations.literal: Gu Hun, style name Yuanchong, was a man of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Hun, whose style name was Yuanchong, came from Changli.

sentences.zh: 父袞，膂力兼人，彎弓三百斤，勇冠一時。

translations.literal: His father Gun had strength surpassing other men, could draw a bow of three hundred jin, and his courage was foremost in his age.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gun had strength beyond ordinary men, could draw a bow weighing three hundred jin, and was accounted the bravest man of his day.

sentences.zh: 仕慕容垂，至廣武將軍。

translations.literal: He served Murong Chui and rose to General of Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Chui and rose to the rank of General of Guangwu.

sentences.zh: 渾正直有操行，性不苟合，趣舍不與己同者，視之蔑如也。

translations.literal: Hun was upright with proper conduct; by nature he would not compromise casually—those whose choices differed from his own he regarded with contempt.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was upright and principled by nature; he would not compromise casually, and those whose choices differed from his own he treated with open contempt.

sentences.zh: 然愛重舊故，不以富貴驕人。

translations.literal: Yet he cherished old friends and did not treat others arrogantly because of wealth and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he cherished old friends and did not lord his wealth and rank over others.

sentences.zh: 時人以此稱之。

translations.literal: People of the time praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 在官廉直，為世祖所器重，詔以渾子孫十五以上悉補中書學生。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and upright and was greatly valued by the Shizu; an edict ordered that all of Hun's descendants aged fifteen and above be appointed students of the Secretariat school.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and incorruptible in office, he won great favor from Emperor Taiwu, who ordered that all of Hun's descendants aged fifteen and above be enrolled as students of the Secretariat school.

sentences.zh: 延和二年春，卒。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Yanhe he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the spring of the second year of the Yanhe era.

sentences.zh: 世祖悼惜之，親臨其喪。

translations.literal: The Shizu mourned him and personally attended his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him and personally attended his funeral.

sentences.zh: 贈賜豐厚，諡曰文宣。

translations.literal: Posthumous gifts were lavish, and his posthumous epithet was Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumous gifts were lavish, and he was given the posthumous epithet Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 子闡，字崇基，小字長命，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Chan, style name Chongji, childhood name Changming, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chan, whose style name was Chongji and childhood name Changming, inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 少侍東宮，稍遷平南將軍、相州刺史。

translations.literal: From youth he attended the Eastern Palace; he was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he served in the Eastern Palace and was gradually promoted to General Who Pacifies the South and governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 入為外都大官。

translations.literal: He entered the court as Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Grand Officer of the Outer Capital.

sentences.zh: 延興四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yanxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Yanxing era.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡公。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Duke Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Duke Jian.

sentences.zh: 闡弟季孫，襲爵。

translations.literal: Chan's younger brother Jisun inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Chan's younger brother Jisun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 中書學生，入為祕書中散，遷中部大夫。

translations.literal: He was a student of the Secretariat school, entered as Secretary Within, and was transferred to Grandee of the Central Section.
translations.idiomatic: He studied at the Secretariat school, entered service as secretary within the palace, and was promoted to Grandee of the Central Section.

sentences.zh: 出為吐京鎮將。

translations.literal: He went out as Garrison General of Tujing.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as garrison general of Tujing.

sentences.zh: 闡子洪，字元孫。

translations.literal: Chan's son Hong, style name Yuansun.
translations.idiomatic: Chan's son Hong, whose style name was Yuansun,

sentences.zh: 少受學中書。

translations.literal: From youth he studied in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he studied in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 世祖以洪機敏有祖風，令入授高宗經。

translations.literal: The Shizu, because Hong was quick-witted and had his grandfather's manner, ordered him to enter and instruct the Gaozong in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu, seeing that Hong was quick-witted and resembled his grandfather in manner, had him enter the palace to instruct Emperor Xiaowen in the classics.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，以舊恩為散騎常侍、南部長。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong took the throne, because of old favor he was made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and Chief of the Southern Section.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen took the throne, Hong was made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and chief of the Southern Section in recognition of old ties.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書，賜爵滎陽公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 洪性貪奢，僕妾衣服錦綺，貲累千金，而求欲滋劇。

translations.literal: Hong was greedy and extravagant; his servants' and concubines' clothes were brocade and silk, his wealth piled up to a thousand gold, and his desires grew ever more intense.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was greedy and extravagant; his servants and concubines wore brocade and silk, his wealth piled up to a thousand gold pieces, and his appetites grew ever sharper.

sentences.zh: 時顯祖舅李峻等初至京師，官給衣服，洪輒截沒。

translations.literal: At that time the Xianzu's uncle-in-law Li Jun and others had just arrived in the capital; the government supplied them with clothes, but Hong intercepted and kept them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen's uncle Li Jun and others first reached the capital, the court supplied them with clothing, but Hong intercepted and kept it.

sentences.zh: 為有司所糾，并窮其前後贓罪，坐以伏法。

translations.literal: He was impeached by the relevant office, and his past and present crimes of corruption were fully investigated; he was executed by law.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant office impeached him, his past and present crimes of corruption were fully investigated, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 子穎，青州、征東大將軍、廣陵王羽田曹參軍，員外散騎侍郎，給事中，尚書郎，加威遠將軍。

translations.literal: His son Ying served as Registrar in the Field and Household Section of Prince Guangling Yu of Qingzhou, Eastern Campaign Grand General, Extraordinary Attendant of the Cavalry, Attendant Within the Yellow Gates, Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, with the additional title General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying served as registrar in the household of Prince Guangling Yu, extraordinary attendant of the cavalry, attendant within the yellow gates, gentleman of the masters of writing, and general who displays might.

sentences.zh: 除員外散騎常侍，尋轉中散大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Extraordinary Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and soon transferred to Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was made extraordinary regular attendant of the cavalry and soon transferred to grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 大軍伐蜀，時益州刺史傅豎眼出為別將，以穎權行州事。

translations.literal: When the great army campaigned against Shu, the Governor of Yizhou Fu Shuyan went out as a separate commander; Ying was entrusted with acting authority over the province.
translations.idiomatic: During the great campaign against Shu, when Governor of Yizhou Fu Shuyan went out as a separate commander, Ying was entrusted with acting authority over the province.

sentences.zh: 後除假節、鎮遠將軍、涼州刺史，不行。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed with provisional staff, General Who Pacifies the Distant, and Governor of Liangzhou, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given provisional staff as General Who Pacifies the Distant and governor of Liangzhou but did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 改授太府少卿，又加前將軍。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury and given the additional title Forward General.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as vice director of the imperial treasury and given the added title Forward General.

sentences.zh: 神龜二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengui he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Shengui era.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、營州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous epithet Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Yingzhou, with the posthumous epithet Zhen.

sentences.zh: 長子纂，字靈紹，頗有學涉。

translations.literal: His eldest son Zuan, style name Lingshao, was fairly learned.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zuan, whose style name was Lingshao, had considerable learning.

sentences.zh: 解褐太學博士，領侍御史。

translations.literal: On leaving the sackcloth he became Erudite of the Imperial Academy and oversaw the attending censor.
translations.idiomatic: On entering service he became erudite of the Imperial Academy and oversaw the attending censor.

sentences.zh: 稍遷著作郎、司州治中、黃門郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Gentleman of the Writing Office, Rectifier of Sizhou, Gentleman of the Yellow Gates, and Regular Attendant of the Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to gentleman of the writing office, rectifier of Sizhou, gentleman of the yellow gates, and regular attendant of the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 又為侍中、兼殿中尚書。

translations.literal: He also served as Palace Attendant and concurrent Minister of the Palace Section.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as palace attendant and concurrent minister of the palace section.

sentences.zh: 遷驃騎大將軍、左光祿大夫、營州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of the Left Household, and Chief Rectifier of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of Agile Cavalry, grand master of the left household, and chief rectifier of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 纂前為著作，又監國史，不能有所緝綴。

translations.literal: Zuan had earlier served in the Writing Office and also supervised the national history, but could accomplish no compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan had earlier served in the writing office and also supervised the national history, but could accomplish no real compilation.

sentences.zh: 纂弟士恢，字紹達。

translations.literal: Zuan's younger brother Shihui, style name Shaoda.
translations.idiomatic: Zuan's younger brother Shihui, whose style name was Shaoda,

sentences.zh: 少好琴書。

translations.literal: From youth he loved the zither and books.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved the zither and books.

sentences.zh: 初為世宗挽郎，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: At first he was a dirge officer for Emperor Xuanwu, then appointed Attendant at Court.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a dirge officer for Emperor Xuanwu, then was appointed attendant at court.

sentences.zh: 正光中，入侍，甚為肅宗寵待。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he entered attendance and was greatly favored by Emperor Xiaoming.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengguang era he entered palace attendance and won great favor from Emperor Xiaoming.

sentences.zh: 元叉之出，靈太后反政，紹達預有力焉。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha was removed and Empress Dowager Ling restored to power, Shaoda had contributed force to the effort.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha was removed and Empress Dowager Ling returned to power, Shaoda had lent significant support.

sentences.zh: 遷諫議大夫，俄轉通直散騎常侍、直閤將軍、鴻臚少卿，封元城縣開國侯，邑七百戶。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Remonstrating Grandee, and soon transferred to Regular Attendant of the Cavalry with Direct Communication, General of the Inner Quarters, Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Relations, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuancheng with a fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to remonstrating grandee, then soon made regular attendant of the cavalry with direct communication, general of the inner quarters, vice director of the court for diplomatic relations, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Yuancheng with a fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太后嬖幸鄭儼，懼紹達間構於帝，每因言次，導紹達為州。

translations.literal: The empress dowager favored Zheng Yan and feared Shaoda would sow discord with the emperor; whenever she spoke with him she steered Shaoda toward a provincial post.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager favored Zheng Yan and feared Shaoda would sow discord with the emperor; whenever she spoke with the emperor she steered Shaoda toward a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 紹達耽寵，不願出外。

translations.literal: Shaoda, clinging to favor, was unwilling to go abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Clinging to court favor, Shaoda was unwilling to leave the capital.

sentences.zh: 太后誣其罪而殺之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager fabricated crimes against him and had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager fabricated charges against him and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 公孫表，字玄元，燕郡廣陽人也。

translations.literal: Gongsun Biao, style name Xuanyuan, was a man of Guangyang in Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Biao, whose style name was Xuanyuan, came from Guangyang in Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 遊學為諸生。

translations.literal: He traveled to study and became a student.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to study and became a student of the classics.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖以為尚書郎。

translations.literal: Murong Chong appointed him Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong appointed him gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂破長子，從入中山。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui took Changzi, he followed him into Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui captured Changzi, Biao followed him into Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶走，乃歸闕。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao fled, he then submitted to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao fled, he submitted to the Wei court.

sentences.zh: 以使江南稱旨，拜尚書郎。

translations.literal: Because his mission to the south of the Yangtze pleased the throne, he was appointed Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mission south of the Yangtze pleased the throne, he was appointed gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 後為博士。

translations.literal: Later he became an Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He later became an erudite.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖以慕容垂諸子分據勢要，權柄推移，遂至亡滅；

translations.literal: Earlier the Taizu had observed that Murong Chui's sons each held strategic posts and as power shifted the state fell to ruin;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Taizu had observed that Murong Chui's sons each held strategic posts and, as power shifted among them, the state fell to ruin;

sentences.zh: 且國俗敦樸，嗜欲寡少，不可啟其機心，而導其巧利，深非之。

translations.literal: moreover the national custom was plain and simple, desires few—one must not stir their scheming minds and lead them toward crafty profit; he deeply disapproved of this.
translations.idiomatic: moreover the national custom was plain and simple and desires were few—one must not stir their scheming minds or lead them toward crafty profit, which he deeply disapproved.

sentences.zh: 表承指上韓非書二十卷，太祖稱善。

translations.literal: Biao, following this intent, presented twenty scrolls of Han Feizi; the Taizu praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, following this intent, presented twenty scrolls of the Han Feizi; the Taizu praised it.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，表參功勞將軍元屈軍事，討吐京叛胡，為胡所敗。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taizong's reign, Biao assisted General of Meritorious Service Yuan Qu in military affairs in suppressing the rebellious Hu of Tujing and was defeated by the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Mingyuan's reign, Biao assisted General of Meritorious Service Yuan Qu in suppressing the rebellious Hu of Tujing and was defeated by them.

sentences.zh: 表以先諫止屈，太宗善之，賜爵固安子。

translations.literal: Biao had earlier remonstrated to stop Qu; the Taizong approved of this and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had earlier remonstrated against Qu's plan; the emperor approved and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 河西飢胡劉虎聚結流民，反於上黨，南寇河內。

translations.literal: The famished Hu of Hexi, Liu Hu, gathered wandering people and rebelled in Shangdang, raiding south into Henei.
translations.idiomatic: The famished Hu of Hexi, Liu Hu, gathered displaced people and rebelled in Shangdang, raiding south into Henei.

sentences.zh: 詔表討虎，又令表與姚興洛陽戍將結期，使備河南岸，然後進軍討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Biao to suppress Hu; he was also ordered to fix a date with Yao Xing's garrison commander at Luoyang so that the south bank of the Yellow River would be secured before advancing to attack.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Biao to suppress Hu and to fix a date with Yao Xing's garrison commander at Luoyang so the south bank of the Yellow River would be secured before the advance.

sentences.zh: 時胡內自疑阻，更相殺害，表以其有解散之勢，遂不與戍將相聞，率眾討之。

translations.literal: At that time the Hu were inwardly suspicious and killed one another; Biao, seeing they were on the verge of disbanding, did not inform the garrison commander and led his troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Hu were inwardly suspicious and killing one another; seeing they were near disbanding, Biao did not inform the garrison commander and led his troops to attack.

sentences.zh: 法令不整，為胡所敗，軍人大被傷殺。

translations.literal: His discipline was not strict; he was defeated by the Hu and many soldiers were killed or wounded.
translations.idiomatic: His discipline was lax; he was defeated by the Hu and many soldiers were killed or wounded.

sentences.zh: 太宗深銜之。

translations.literal: The Taizong deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 及劉裕征姚興，兗州刺史尉建聞寇至，棄滑臺北走，詔表隨壽光侯叔孫建屯枋頭。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu campaigned against Yao Xing, the Governor of Yanzhou Wei Jian, hearing the enemy had arrived, abandoned Huatai and fled north; an edict ordered Biao to follow the Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian in garrisoning Fangtou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu campaigned against Yao Xing, Governor of Yanzhou Wei Jian, hearing the enemy had arrived, abandoned Huatai and fled north; Biao was ordered to follow Marquis of Shouguang Shusun Jian in garrisoning Fangtou.

sentences.zh: 泰常七年，劉裕死，議取河南侵地。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taichang, Liu Yu died; there was discussion of taking the invaded lands south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Taichang, Liu Yu died, and the court discussed recovering the invaded lands south of the river.

sentences.zh: 太宗以為掠地至淮，滑臺等三城自然面縛。

translations.literal: The Taizong thought that if they seized territory as far as the Huai, Huatai and the other three cities would naturally submit of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought that if they seized territory as far as the Huai, Huatai and the other three cities would submit of themselves.

sentences.zh: 表固執宜先攻城，太宗從之。

translations.literal: Biao firmly insisted they should attack the cities first; the Taizong followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Biao firmly insisted they should attack the cities first, and the emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 於是以奚斤為都督，以表為吳兵將軍、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Xi Jin was made commander; Biao was made General of Wu Troops and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin was made overall commander; Biao was made General of Wu Troops and governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 斤等濟河，表攻滑臺，歷時不拔。

translations.literal: Jin and others crossed the river; Biao attacked Huatai but could not take it for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and others crossed the river; Biao attacked Huatai but could not take it for a long time.

sentences.zh: 太宗乃南巡，為之聲援。

translations.literal: The Taizong then toured south to support them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then toured south to support them.

sentences.zh: 表等既克滑臺，引師西伐，大破劉義隆將翟廣等於土樓，[6]遂圍虎牢。

translations.literal: After Biao and the others took Huatai, they led the army west and greatly defeated Liu Yilong's general Zhai Guang and others at Tulou, [6] then besieged Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: After Biao and the others took Huatai, they marched west and greatly defeated Liu Yilong's general Zhai Guang and others at Tulou, [6] then besieged Hulao.

sentences.zh: 車駕次汲郡，始昌子蘇坦、太史令王亮奏表置軍虎牢東，不得利便之地，故令賊不時滅。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted in Ji commandery; Viscount of Shichang Su Tan and Court Astronomer Wang Liang memorialized that Biao had placed his army east of Hulao, not in an advantageous position, and so the bandits were not quickly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage halted in Ji commandery; Su Tan, Viscount of Shichang, and Court Astronomer Wang Liang memorialized that Biao had placed his army east of Hulao, not in an advantageous position, and so the enemy was not quickly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 太宗雅好術數，又積前忿，及攻虎牢，士卒多傷，乃使人夜就帳中縊而殺之。

translations.literal: The Taizong had always loved divination and also harbored old resentment; when attacking Hulao many soldiers were wounded, so he sent men at night into the tent to strangle and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always loved divination and also harbored old resentment; when the attack on Hulao cost many soldiers' lives, he sent men at night into Biao's tent to strangle him.

sentences.zh: 時年六十四。

translations.literal: He was then sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 太宗以賊未退，祕而不宣。

translations.literal: Because the bandits had not yet retreated, this was kept secret.
translations.idiomatic: Because the enemy had not yet retreated, the death was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 初，表與勃海封愷友善，後為子求愷從女，愷不許，表甚銜之。

translations.literal: Earlier Biao had been friendly with Feng Kai of Bohai; later he sought Kai's cousin's daughter for his son, but Kai refused, and Biao deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Biao had been friendly with Feng Kai of Bohai; later he sought Kai's cousin's daughter for his son, but Kai refused, and Biao deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 及封氏為司馬國璠所逮，太宗以舊族欲原之，表固證其罪，乃誅封氏。

translations.literal: When the Feng clan was seized by Sima Guofan, the Taizong wished to pardon them as an old family; Biao firmly proved their guilt, and the Feng clan was executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Feng clan was seized by Sima Guofan, the emperor wished to pardon them as an old family; Biao firmly proved their guilt, and the Feng clan was executed.

sentences.zh: 表為人外和內忌，時人以此薄之。

translations.literal: Biao was outwardly harmonious but inwardly jealous; people of the time looked down on him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was outwardly agreeable but inwardly jealous; people of the time looked down on him for this.

sentences.zh: 表本與王亮同營署，及其出也，輕侮亮，故至於死。

translations.literal: Biao had originally been in the same office as Wang Liang; when Liang went out on assignment, Biao treated him with contempt, and so Liang brought about his death.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had originally served in the same office as Wang Liang; when Liang went out on assignment, Biao treated him with contempt, and so Liang brought about his death.

sentences.zh: 第二子軌，字元慶。

translations.literal: His second son Gui, style name Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Gui, whose style name was Yuanqing,

sentences.zh: 少以文學知名，太宗時為中書郎。

translations.literal: From youth he was famed for literary learning; in the Taizong's time he was Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was famed for literary learning; in Emperor Mingyuan's time he served as gentleman of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 出從征討，補諸軍司馬。

translations.literal: He went out following campaigns and was appointed military aide to the various armies.
translations.idiomatic: He went out on campaigns and was appointed military aide to the various armies.

sentences.zh: 世祖平赫連昌，引諸將帥入其府藏，各令任意取金玉。

translations.literal: When the Shizu pacified Helian Chang, he led the generals into the prince's treasury and let each take gold and jade as he wished.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu pacified Helian Chang, he led the generals into the prince's treasury and let each take gold and jade as he wished.

sentences.zh: 諸將取之盈懷，軌獨不探把。

translations.literal: The generals filled their arms; Gui alone did not reach out.
translations.idiomatic: The generals filled their arms; Gui alone did not reach out.

sentences.zh: 世祖乃親探金賜之，謂軌曰：「卿可謂臨財不苟得，朕所以增賜者，欲顯廉於眾人。」

translations.literal: The Shizu then personally took gold and gave it to him, saying to Gui: "You may be said not to grasp at wealth when facing it; the reason I add this gift is to display integrity before the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then personally took gold and gave it to him, saying: "You may be said not to grasp at wealth when facing it; the reason I add this gift is to display integrity before everyone."

sentences.zh: 後兼大鴻臚，持節拜氐王楊玄為南秦王。

translations.literal: Later he was also made Grand Master of the Court for Diplomatic Relations, bearing the staff to invest the Di king Yang Xuan as King of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He later also served as grand master of the court for diplomatic relations, bearing the staff to invest the Di king Yang Xuan as King of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 及境，玄不郊迎，軌數玄曰：「昔尉他跨據，及陸賈至，匍匐奉順，故能垂名竹帛。

translations.literal: When he reached the border, Xuan did not come out to meet him in the suburbs; Gui rebuked Xuan: "In former times Zhao Tuo held his own territory; when Lu Jia arrived, he prostrated himself in submission and so his name was recorded on bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the border, Xuan did not come out to meet him in the suburbs; Gui rebuked him: "In former times Zhao Tuo held his own territory apart; when Lu Jia arrived, he prostrated himself in submission and so his name was recorded for posterity.

sentences.zh: 今君王無肅恭之禮，非蕃臣也。

translations.literal: Now the king lacks the ceremony of respectful submission—he is no vassal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty lacks the ceremony of respectful submission—you are no vassal minister."

sentences.zh: 」玄使其屬趙客子對曰：「天子以六合為家，孰非王庭，是以敢請入國，然後受謁。

translations.literal: Xuan had his subordinate Zhao Kezi reply: "The Son of Heaven takes the six directions as his house—what place is not his court? Therefore I dare request to enter the state and then receive audience."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had his subordinate Zhao Kezi reply: "The Son of Heaven takes the six directions as his house—what place is not his court? Therefore I dare request to enter the state and then receive audience."

sentences.zh: 」軌答曰：「大夫入境，尚有郊勞，而況王命者乎？

translations.literal: Gui answered: "When a grandee enters a state, there is still suburban greeting—how much more when one bears the king's command?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui answered: "When a grandee enters a state, there is still suburban greeting—how much more when one bears the king's command?"

sentences.zh: 請奉策以還。

translations.literal: Please take the investiture document and return."
translations.idiomatic: Please take the investiture document and return."

sentences.zh: 」玄懼，詣郊受命。

translations.literal: Xuan was afraid and went to the suburbs to receive the command.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was afraid and went to the suburbs to receive the command.

sentences.zh: 軌使還，稱旨，拜尚書，賜爵燕郡公，加平南將軍。

translations.literal: When Gui returned and his mission pleased the throne, he was appointed Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan commandery, and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui returned and his mission pleased the throne, he was appointed minister of works, enfeoffed as Duke of Yan commandery, and given the added title General Who Pacifies the South.

sentences.zh: 及劉義隆將到彥之遣其部將姚縱夫濟河，攻冶坂。
