translations.literal: When Liu Yilong's general Dao Yanzhi sent his subordinate Yao Zongfu across the river to attack Yebai.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yilong's general Dao Yanzhi sent his subordinate Yao Zongfu across the river to attack Yebai.

sentences.zh: 世祖慮更北入，遣軌屯壺關。

translations.literal: The Shizu feared a further push north and sent Gui to garrison Huguan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared a further push north and sent Gui to garrison Huguan.

sentences.zh: 會上黨丁零叛，軌討平之。

translations.literal: At that time the Dingling of Shangdang rebelled; Gui suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Dingling of Shangdang rebelled; Gui suppressed and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 出為虎牢鎮將。

translations.literal: He went out as Garrison General of Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as garrison general of Hulao.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖將北征，發民驢以運糧，使軌部詣雍州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Shizu was about to campaign north, he mobilized the people's donkeys to transport grain and sent Gui's section to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the emperor was about to campaign north, he mobilized the people's donkeys to transport grain and sent Gui's section to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 軌令驢主皆加絹一匹，乃與受之。

translations.literal: Gui ordered each donkey owner to add one bolt of silk, and only then accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Gui ordered each donkey owner to add one bolt of silk, and only then accepted them.

sentences.zh: 百姓為之語曰：「驢無強弱，輔脊自壯。

translations.literal: The people made a saying: "Donkeys have no strong or weak—the assistant's back is always stout."
translations.idiomatic: The people made a saying: "Donkeys have no strong or weak—the assistant's back is always stout."

sentences.zh: 」[7]眾共嗤之。

translations.literal: The multitude all mocked him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone mocked him for this.

sentences.zh: 坐徵還。

translations.literal: He was summoned back for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned back for investigation.

sentences.zh: 真君二年卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenjun he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Zhenjun era, aged fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 軌既死，世祖謂崔浩曰：「吾行過上黨，父老皆曰：公孫軌為受貨縱賊，使至今餘姦不除，軌之咎也。

translations.literal: After Gui died, the Shizu said to Cui Hao: "When I passed through Shangdang, the elders all said Gongsun Gui accepted bribes and indulged bandits, so that evildoers remain uncleaned to this day—that is Gui's fault.
translations.idiomatic: After Gui died, the emperor said to Cui Hao: "When I passed through Shangdang, the elders all said Gongsun Gui accepted bribes and indulged bandits, so evildoers remain to this day—that is Gui's fault.

sentences.zh: 其初來，單馬執鞭；

translations.literal: When he first came, he rode alone with whip in hand;
translations.idiomatic: When he first came, he rode alone with whip in hand;

sentences.zh: 返去，從車百兩，載物而南。

translations.literal: when he returned, a hundred carts followed, loaded with goods going south.
translations.idiomatic: when he returned, a hundred carts followed, loaded with goods going south.

sentences.zh: 丁零渠帥乘山罵軌，軌怒，取罵者之母，以矛刺其陰而殺之，曰：『何以生此逆子！

translations.literal: A Dingling chieftain on the mountain cursed Gui; Gui in anger took the curser's mother, stabbed her private parts with a spear and killed her, saying: 'Why give birth to this rebellious son!'
translations.idiomatic: A Dingling chieftain on the mountain cursed Gui; Gui in anger took the curser's mother, stabbed her private parts with a spear and killed her, saying: 'Why give birth to this rebellious son!'

sentences.zh: 』從下到擘，分磔四支於山樹上以肆其忿。

translations.literal: From below upward he dismembered her, quartering the four limbs on mountain trees to vent his rage.
translations.idiomatic: From below upward he dismembered her, quartering the four limbs on mountain trees to vent his rage.

sentences.zh: 是忍行不忍之事。

translations.literal: This was doing what the humane cannot bear to do.
translations.idiomatic: This was doing what the humane cannot bear to do.

sentences.zh: 軌幸而早死，至今在者，吾必族而誅之。」

translations.literal: Gui had the luck to die young; had he still been alive today, I would surely have exterminated his entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune spared Gui an early death—had he lived until today, I would have wiped out his whole clan.

sentences.zh: 軌終得娶于封氏，生二子，斌、叡。

translations.literal: Gui ultimately succeeded in marrying into the Feng clan and fathered two sons, Bin and Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Gui eventually married into the Feng clan and had two sons, Bin and Rui.

sentences.zh: 斌，襲爵。

translations.literal: Bin inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Bin succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 拜內都大官。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand Officer of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand officer of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 正光二年卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Zhengguang era.

sentences.zh: [8]贈幽州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Governor of Youzhou. [8]
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made governor of Youzhou. [8]

sentences.zh: 叡，字文叔。

translations.literal: Rui, style name Wenshu.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, whose style name was Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 初為東宮吏，稍遷儀曹長，賜爵陽平公。

translations.literal: At first he was an officer of the Eastern Palace; he was gradually promoted to Chief of the Bureau of Ceremonial and enfeoffed as Duke of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an officer in the Eastern Palace, was gradually promoted to chief of the Bureau of Ceremonial, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 時顯祖於苑內立殿，敕中秘羣官制名。

translations.literal: At that time the Xianzu built a hall within the imperial park and ordered the secretariat officials to devise a name.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Xianzu built a hall in the imperial park and ordered secretariat officials to choose a name for it.

sentences.zh: 叡曰：「臣聞至尊至貴，莫崇於帝王；

translations.literal: Rui said: "I have heard that among the most exalted and noble, none is loftier than the emperor and king;
translations.idiomatic: Rui said, "I have heard that nothing ranks above the emperor among the most exalted and noble;

sentences.zh: 天人挹損，莫大于謙光。

translations.literal: among Heaven and man in self-restraint, nothing is greater than modest humility.
translations.idiomatic: and that among all forms of restraint suited to Heaven and man, nothing surpasses modest humility.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下躬唐虞之德，存道頤神，逍遙物外，宮居之名，當協叡旨。

translations.literal: I consider that Your Majesty embodies the virtue of Tang and Yu, preserves the Way and nourishes the spirit, roaming free beyond worldly affairs—the name of the palace dwelling should accord with profound meaning.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly consider that Your Majesty embodies the virtue of the sage-kings Tang and Yu, preserves the Way and nourishes the spirit, and roams free beyond worldly affairs—the hall's name should reflect that profound intent.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為宜曰『崇光』。

translations.literal: This subject in his folly believes it should be called "Chongguang" ("Exalted Radiance").
translations.idiomatic: In my humble opinion, it should be called "Chongguang"—"Exalted Radiance."

sentences.zh: 」奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 後卒於南部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he died while serving as Minister of the Southern Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He later died while serving as Minister of the Southern Branch.

sentences.zh: 贈安東將軍、幽州刺史，諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the East and governor of Youzhou, with the posthumous name Xuan.

sentences.zh: 叡妻，崔浩弟女也，生子良，字遵伯。

translations.literal: Rui's wife was the daughter of Cui Hao's younger brother; she bore a son Liang, style name Zunbo.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's wife was a daughter of Cui Hao's younger brother; she bore a son named Liang, whose style name was Zunbo.

sentences.zh: 聰明好學，為尚書左丞，雅有幹用，為高祖所知遇。

translations.literal: Intelligent and fond of learning, he became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was naturally capable in affairs, and was recognized and favored by the Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent and studious, he became Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; naturally capable in affairs, he won the Gaozu's recognition and favor.

sentences.zh: 良弟衡，字道津。

translations.literal: Liang's younger brother Heng, style name Daojin.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's younger brother Heng had the style name Daojin.

sentences.zh: 良推爵讓之，仕至司直。

translations.literal: Liang yielded his title to him, and he served up to Grand Corrector.
translations.idiomatic: Liang renounced his title in Heng's favor, and Heng rose to the post of Grand Corrector.

sentences.zh: 良以別功，賜爵昌平子。

translations.literal: Liang, for separate merits, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, for separate achievements, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Changping.

sentences.zh: 子崇基襲。

translations.literal: His son Chongji inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongji succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 軌弟質，字元直。

translations.literal: Gui's younger brother Zhi, style name Yuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's younger brother Zhi had the style name Yuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 有經義，頗屬文。

translations.literal: He had learning in the classics and was quite literate.
translations.idiomatic: He was well versed in the classics and reasonably accomplished as a writer.

sentences.zh: 初為中書學生，稍遷博士。

translations.literal: At first he was a student of the Secretariat; he was gradually promoted to Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a student in the Secretariat and was gradually promoted to the rank of erudite.

sentences.zh: 世祖征涼州，留宜都王穆壽輔恭宗。

translations.literal: When the Shizu campaigned against Liangzhou, he left Prince Yidu Mu Shou to assist the Gongzong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu campaigned against Liangzhou, he left Prince Yidu Mu Shou behind to assist the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時蠕蠕乘虛犯塞，候騎至於京師，京師大震。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran seized the opportunity to raid the frontier; scouts reached the capital, and the capital was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Rouran seized the opportunity to raid the frontier; advance scouts reached the capital, and the city was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 壽雅信任質，以為謀主。

translations.literal: Shou greatly trusted Zhi and made him his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Shou trusted Zhi deeply and relied on him as his chief adviser.

sentences.zh: 質性好卜筮，卜筮者咸云寇必不來，故不謀備。

translations.literal: Zhi's nature was fond of divination; the diviners all said the invaders would surely not come, so they made no plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was fond of divination; the diviners all declared the enemy would not come, so no defensive preparations were made.

sentences.zh: 由質幾致敗國。

translations.literal: Because of Zhi they nearly brought ruin to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's influence nearly brought the state to ruin.

sentences.zh: 後深自督厲，屢進讜言，超遷尚書。

translations.literal: Later he deeply disciplined himself, repeatedly offered forthright counsel, and was exceptionally promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Later he redoubled his self-discipline, repeatedly offered forthright counsel, and was rapidly promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 真君九年卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenjun he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of the Zhenjun era.

sentences.zh: 追贈中護軍將軍、光祿勳、幽州刺史、廣陽侯，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles General of the Central Guard, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Governor of Youzhou, and Marquis of Guangyang, with the posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General of the Central Guard, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, governor of Youzhou, and Marquis of Guangyang, with the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 第二子邃，字文慶。

translations.literal: The second son Sui, style name Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Sui had the style name Wenqing.

sentences.zh: 初為選部吏，以積勤，稍遷南部長。

translations.literal: At first he was an officer of the Selection Bureau; through accumulated diligent service he was gradually promoted to Chief of the Southern Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an officer in the Selection Bureau and, through sustained diligent service, was gradually promoted to chief of the Southern Branch.

sentences.zh: 敷奏有稱，遷南部尚書，賜爵范陽侯，加左將軍。

translations.literal: His memorials won praise; he was promoted to Minister of the Southern Branch, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang, and given the additional title of General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials were well regarded; he was promoted to Minister of the Southern Branch, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fanyang, and given the added title of General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 高祖詔邃與內都幢將、上谷公張儵率眾討蕭賾舞陰戍。

translations.literal: The Gaozu ordered Sui, together with the Inner Command Standard-Bearer Zhang Su, Duke of Shanggu, to lead troops to attack Xiao Ze's fortress at Wuyin.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu ordered Sui, together with the Inner Command standard-bearer Zhang Su, Duke of Shanggu, to lead troops against Xiao Ze's fortress at Wuyin.

sentences.zh: 後高祖與文明太后引見王公以下，高祖曰：「比年方割畿內及京城三部，於百姓頗有益否？

translations.literal: Later the Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming summoned and received the princes and dukes and those below them; the Gaozu said: "In recent years we partitioned the capital region and the three districts of the capital—has this been of much benefit to the common people?
translations.idiomatic: Later the Gaozu and Empress Dowager Wenming received the princes, dukes, and officials below them, and the Gaozu asked, "In recent years we partitioned the capital region and the three metropolitan districts—has this benefited the common people?

sentences.zh: 」邃對曰：「先者人民離散，主司猥多，至於督察，實難齊整。

translations.literal: Sui replied: "Formerly the people were scattered and the supervising offices were excessively numerous; as for oversight, it was truly hard to keep in order.
translations.idiomatic: Sui replied, "Previously the populace was scattered and supervisory offices were far too numerous—overseeing them was genuinely difficult.

sentences.zh: 自方割以來，眾賦易辦，實有大益。

translations.literal: Since the partition, public levies have been easy to handle—there has truly been great benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Since the partition, tax collection has been much easier, and the benefits have been substantial.

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「諸人多言無益，卿言可謂識治機矣。

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Many people say it was of no benefit; your words may be called knowing the moment for governance.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Most people say it was useless—but your answer shows you understand the right moment for governance.

sentences.zh: 」詔醴陽被掠之兵，有得還者，賜絹二十匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that soldiers of Liyang who had been captured and subsequently returned be granted twenty bolts of silk each.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted twenty bolts of silk to each soldier of Liyang who had been captured and later returned.

sentences.zh: 邃奏為貴賤等級，高祖稱善。

translations.literal: Sui memorialized setting grades of noble and base; the Gaozu praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Sui proposed graded distinctions between high and low, which the Gaozu praised.

sentences.zh: 依例降侯，改為襄平伯。

translations.literal: According to precedent his marquisate was reduced, and he was changed to Baron of Xiangping.
translations.idiomatic: Following precedent, his marquisate was reduced and he was made Baron of Xiangping.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、安東將軍、青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as bearer of the staff of authority, General Who Pacifies the East, and governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 以邃在公遺迹可紀，下詔褒述。

translations.literal: Because Sui's public deeds were worth recording, an edict was issued praising and recounting them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sui's public service left a record worth noting, an edict was issued praising his achievements.

sentences.zh: 加鎮東將軍，領東夷校尉，刺史如故。

translations.literal: He was given the additional titles General Who Guards the East and Colonel of the Eastern Barbarians; his governorship remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the added titles of General Who Guards the East and Colonel of the Eastern Barbarians, while retaining his governorship.

sentences.zh: 太和十九年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Taihe he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the nineteenth year of the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 高祖在鄴宮，為之舉哀。

translations.literal: The Gaozu was at the palace in Ye and held mourning rites for him.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozu was at the palace in Ye and held mourning rites for him.

sentences.zh: 時百度唯新，青州佐吏疑為所服。

translations.literal: At that time all institutions were being reformed anew, and the Qingzhou assistants and clerks were uncertain what mourning garments to wear.
translations.idiomatic: Institutions were being comprehensively reformed at the time, and Qingzhou's staff were unsure what mourning garments they should wear.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「今古時殊，禮或隆殺。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Present and ancient times differ, and rites may be heightened or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated, "Times have changed since antiquity, and rites may be heightened or reduced accordingly.

sentences.zh: 專古也，理與今違；

translations.literal: To adhere exclusively to antiquity—its principles conflict with the present;
translations.idiomatic: Follow antiquity alone, and its principles clash with the present;

sentences.zh: 專今也，大乖曩義。

translations.literal: to adhere exclusively to the present—this greatly departs from past meaning.
translations.idiomatic: follow the present alone, and you abandon the spirit of the past.

sentences.zh: 當斟酌兩途，商量得失，吏民之情亦不可苟順也。

translations.literal: One should weigh both paths and consider gains and losses—the feelings of officials and commoners likewise cannot be casually indulged.
translations.idiomatic: Both paths must be weighed and their gains and losses considered—the feelings of officials and commoners cannot be casually indulged either.

sentences.zh: 主簿，近代相承服斬，過葬便除，可如故事。

translations.literal: For chief clerks, in recent generations the successive practice has been to wear the highest mourning until after burial, then end mourning—this may follow precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks, by recent custom, wear the highest grade of mourning until after burial and then end it—that precedent may be followed.

sentences.zh: 自餘無服，大成寥落，可準諸境內之民，為齊衰三月。」

translations.literal: For the rest, who wear no mourning, a great assembly would be too sparse—let them follow the common people within the jurisdiction and wear second-grade mourning for three months.
translations.idiomatic: For everyone else, who would wear no mourning at all, a full assembly would be too sparse—they may follow the common people of the region and wear second-grade mourning for three months."

sentences.zh: 子同始，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Tongshi inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tongshi succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 卒於給事中。

translations.literal: He died while serving as Attendant Within the Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Attendant Within the Gates.

sentences.zh: 同始弟同慶，篤厚廉慎，為司徒田曹參軍，李崇驃騎府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Tongshi's younger brother Tongqing was sincere, honest, and cautious; he served as Adjunct of the Field Bureau under the Minister of Works and as Outer Troops Adjunct in Li Chong's Rapid Cavalry Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Tongshi's younger brother Tongqing was sincere, honest, and cautious; he served as an adjunct in the Field Bureau under the Minister of Works and as an outer-troop adjutant in Li Chong's Rapid Cavalry headquarters.

sentences.zh: 隨崇北征，有方直之稱。

translations.literal: Following Chong on the northern campaign, he won a reputation for integrity and forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: On Li Chong's northern campaign he earned a reputation for integrity and forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 邃、叡為從父兄弟，而叡才器小優，又封氏之生，崔氏之壻，邃母雁門李氏，地望縣隔。

translations.literal: Sui and Rui were cousins by the paternal line, yet Rui's talent and capacity were slightly superior; moreover, he was born of the Feng clan and married into the Cui clan, while Sui's mother was the Li clan of Yanmen—their family standing was widely separated.
translations.idiomatic: Sui and Rui were paternal cousins, yet Rui was slightly more talented and capable; moreover, he was born of the Feng clan and married into the Cui clan, while Sui's mother came from the Li clan of Yanmen—their family standing was worlds apart.

sentences.zh: 鉅鹿太守祖季真，多識北方人物，每云：「士大夫當須好婚親，二公孫同堂兄弟耳，吉凶會集，便有士庶之異。」

translations.literal: Zu Jizhen, Governor of Julu, who knew many northern figures, often said: "Scholar-officials must have good marriage alliances—though the two Gongsun are brothers of the same hall, when fortune or misfortune brings them together, there is already the difference of gentleman and commoner."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Jizhen, governor of Julu, who knew many notables of the north, often remarked, "A scholar-official needs a good marriage alliance—the two Gongsuns are brothers under the same roof, yet when they gather for joy or sorrow, the gulf between gentleman and commoner is already plain to see."

sentences.zh: 張濟，字士度，西河人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, style name Shidu, was a man of Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, whose style name was Shidu, came from Xihe.

sentences.zh: 父千秋，慕容永驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: His father Qianqiu was Murong Yong's General of Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qianqiu had served as Murong Yong's General of Valiant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 永滅，來奔。

translations.literal: When Yong was destroyed, he came to defect.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Yong fell, he came over to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 太祖善之，拜建節將軍，賜爵成紀侯。

translations.literal: The Taizu was pleased with him, appointed him General Who Establishes Authority, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chengji.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu welcomed him, appointed him General Who Establishes Authority, and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Chengji.

sentences.zh: 隨從征伐，[9]累著功績。

translations.literal: Following on campaigns, he repeatedly achieved meritorious deeds. [9]
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor on campaign and repeatedly distinguished himself. [9]

sentences.zh: 登國末，卒。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dengguo era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the end of the Dengguo era.

sentences.zh: 濟涉獵書傳，清辯，美儀容。

translations.literal: Ji ranged widely through books and chronicles, was clear in disputation, and had fine bearing and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was widely read in books and chronicles, clear and persuasive in debate, and handsome in bearing.

sentences.zh: 太祖愛之，引侍左右，與公孫表等俱為行人，拜散騎侍郎，襲爵。

translations.literal: The Taizu favored him, kept him in attendance at his side, and together with Gongsun Biao and others he served as envoy; he was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu favored him and kept him in attendance; together with Gongsun Biao and others he served as a diplomatic envoy, was appointed Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant, and succeeded to his father's title.

sentences.zh: 先是，姚興遣將攻洛陽，司馬德宗雍州刺史楊佺期遣使乞師於常山王遵，遵以狀聞，太祖遣濟為遵從事中郎報之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yao Xing had sent a general to attack Luoyang; Sima Dezong's Governor of Yongzhou Yang Quanqi sent an envoy to beg troops from Prince Changshan Zun; Zun reported the situation, and the Taizu sent Ji as Zun's Attendant Gentleman to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yao Xing had sent a general to attack Luoyang; Yang Quanqi, governor of Yongzhou under Sima Dezong, sent an envoy to Prince Changshan Zun to request aid; Zun reported this to the court, and the Taizu sent Ji as an attendant gentleman under Zun to reply.

sentences.zh: 濟自襄陽還，太祖問濟江南之事，濟對曰：「司馬昌明死，子德宗代立，所部州鎮，迭相攻擊，今雖小定，君弱臣強，全無綱紀。

translations.literal: When Ji returned from Xiangyang, the Taizu asked him about affairs south of the Yangzi; Ji replied: "Sima Changming is dead and his son Dezong has succeeded; the prefectures and garrisons under his rule attack one another in turn. Though there is now a slight calm, the ruler is weak and ministers strong—there is no order whatsoever.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji returned from Xiangyang, the Taizu asked him about affairs in the south; Ji replied, "Sima Changming is dead and his son Dezong has taken the throne; the prefectures and garrisons under his rule take turns attacking one another. There is a brief lull now, but the ruler is weak and his ministers are strong—there is no order at all.

sentences.zh: 臣等既至襄陽，佺期問臣：『魏初伐中山幾十萬眾？

translations.literal: When we reached Xiangyang, Quanqi asked me: "When Wei first attacked Zhongshan, how many tens of thousands of troops were there?
translations.idiomatic: When we reached Xiangyang, Quanqi asked me, "When Wei first attacked Zhongshan, how many tens of thousands of troops did you field?

sentences.zh: 』臣答：『三十餘萬。

translations.literal: I answered: "More than three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: I answered, "More than three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 』佺期曰：『魏國被甲戎馬，可有幾匹？

translations.literal: Quanqi said: "How many armored warriors and war-horses does Wei have?
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi said, "How many armored soldiers and war-horses does Wei have?

sentences.zh: 』臣答：『中軍精騎十有餘萬，外軍無數。

translations.literal: I answered: "The central army has more than one hundred thousand elite cavalry; the outer armies are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: I answered, "The central army alone has more than a hundred thousand elite cavalry; the frontier armies are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 』佺期曰：『以此討羌，豈足滅也。

translations.literal: Quanqi said: "With this force to suppress the Qiang, how could it suffice for their destruction?
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi said, "With a force like that against the Qiang, how could you possibly wipe them out?

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『魏定中山，徙幾戶於北？

translations.literal: He also said: "When Wei secured Zhongshan, how many households were moved north?
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, "When Wei secured Zhongshan, how many households did you move north?

sentences.zh: 』臣答：『七萬餘家。

translations.literal: I answered: "More than seventy thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: I answered, "More than seventy thousand households.

sentences.zh: 』佺期曰：『治在何城？

translations.literal: Quanqi said: "In which city is the government centered?
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi asked, "Which city is your capital?

sentences.zh: 』臣答：『定都平城。

translations.literal: I answered: "The fixed capital is Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: I answered, "The capital is fixed at Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 』佺期曰：『有如許大眾，亦何用城為？

translations.literal: Quanqi said: "With so vast a multitude, what need is there for a city?
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi said, "With a population that large, what need is there for a walled capital?

sentences.zh: 』又曰：『魏帝為欲久都平城，將復遷乎？

translations.literal: He also said: "Does the Wei emperor wish to remain long at Pingcheng, or will he move the capital again?
translations.idiomatic: He also asked, "Does the Wei emperor plan to stay at Pingcheng permanently, or will he move the capital again?

sentences.zh: 』臣答：『非所知也。

translations.literal: I answered: "That is not what I know.
translations.idiomatic: I answered, "That is not for me to know.

sentences.zh: 』佺期聞朝廷不都山東，貌有喜色，曰：『晉魏通和，乃在往昔，非唯今日。

translations.literal: When Quanqi heard that the court would not establish its capital in Shandong, his countenance showed pleasure, and he said: "Jin and Wei have been on friendly terms since old times—not only today.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanqi heard that the court had no plans to establish its capital in Shandong, he looked pleased and said, "Jin and Wei have been on friendly terms since long ago—not just today.

sentences.zh: 羌寇狡猾，頻侵河洛，夙夜憂危。

translations.literal: The Qiang raiders are cunning and frequently invade the He and Luo regions; day and night we live in fear and peril.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang raiders are cunning and raid the Heluo region again and again—we live in constant fear.

sentences.zh: 今此寡弱，倉庫空竭，與君便為一家，義所無諱。

translations.literal: Now we here are weak, our storehouses empty and exhausted—we and you are as one family; there is nothing propriety forbids us to speak frankly.
translations.idiomatic: We are weak now, our storehouses empty—we and you are as one family, and there is nothing I need hide from you.

sentences.zh: 洛城救援，仰恃於魏，若獲保全，當必厚報。

translations.literal: Rescue of Luoyang depends on Wei; if it can be preserved, I shall surely requite you generously.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's rescue depends entirely on Wei; if the city is preserved, I will repay you generously.

sentences.zh: 如其為羌所乘，寧使魏取。

translations.literal: If it should be seized by the Qiang, I would rather let Wei take it.
translations.idiomatic: If the Qiang should seize it, I would rather see Wei take it instead.

sentences.zh: 』臣等欲分向揚州。

translations.literal: We wished to split up and go toward Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: We planned to split up and proceed toward Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 佺期曰：『蠻賊互起，水行甚難，魏之軍馬，已據滑臺，於此而還，從北道東下，乃更便直。

translations.literal: Quanqi said: "Barbarian bandits rise everywhere; travel by water is very difficult. Wei's troops and horses already hold Huatai—if you turn back from here and go eastward by the northern route, that will be more convenient and direct.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqi said, "Bandits are rising everywhere, and travel by water is very dangerous. Wei's army already holds Huatai—from here you should turn back and take the northern route east; that will be much easier.

sentences.zh: 晉之法制，有異於魏。

translations.literal: Jin's laws and institutions differ from Wei's.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's laws and institutions differ from yours.

sentences.zh: 今都督襄陽，委以外事，有欲征討，輒便興發，然後表聞，令朝廷知之而已。

translations.literal: The present commander at Xiangyang is entrusted with external affairs—when he wishes to campaign, he simply mobilizes, then memorializes afterward merely so the court is informed.
translations.idiomatic: The commander at Xiangyang now has charge of external affairs—when he wishes to campaign, he simply mobilizes and only afterward notifies the court so it knows what he has done.

sentences.zh: 如其事勢不舉，亦不承臺命。

translations.literal: If the situation does not warrant action, he likewise does not await orders from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: If the situation does not warrant action, he does not wait for orders from the capital either.

sentences.zh: 』」太祖嘉其辭順，乃厚賞其使，許救洛陽。

translations.literal: The Taizu approved his compliant language, richly rewarded the envoy, and agreed to rescue Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu was pleased with his accommodating tone, richly rewarded the envoy, and agreed to rescue Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後遷謁者僕射，報使姚興。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Supervisor of Ushers and sent as envoy to reply to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Supervisor of Ushers and sent as envoy to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 以累使稱旨，拜勝兵將軍。

translations.literal: Because his repeated missions accorded with the imperial will, he was appointed General of Victorious Troops.
translations.idiomatic: Because his repeated embassies pleased the emperor, he was appointed General of Victorious Troops.

sentences.zh: 頻從車駕北伐，濟謀功居多。

translations.literal: He frequently followed the imperial carriage on northern campaigns; in planning Ji contributed the greater share of merit.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently accompanied the emperor on northern campaigns and contributed the lion's share of strategic planning.

sentences.zh: 賞賜奴婢百口，馬牛數百，羊二十餘口。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with a hundred slaves male and female, several hundred horses and cattle, and more than twenty sheep.
translations.idiomatic: He was rewarded with a hundred slaves, several hundred horses and cattle, and more than twenty sheep.

sentences.zh: 天賜五年卒，子多羅襲爵。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianci he died; his son Duoluo inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of the Tianci era; his son Duoluo succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 坐事除。

translations.literal: He was dismissed from office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 李先，字容仁，中山盧奴人也，本字犯高祖廟諱。

translations.literal: Li Xian, style name Rongren, was a man of Lunu in Zhongshan; his original style name violated the taboo of the Gaozu's ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, whose style name was Rongren, came from Lunu in Zhongshan; his original style name had violated the taboo of the Gaozu's ancestral temple name.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善占相之術，師事清河張御，御奇之。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and was skilled in physiognomy and divination; he studied under Zhang Yu of Qinghe, and Yu regarded him as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning and was skilled in physiognomy and divination; he studied under Zhang Yu of Qinghe, who recognized his exceptional talent.

sentences.zh: 仕苻堅，尚書郎。

translations.literal: He served Fu Jian as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served Fu Jian of Former Qin as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 後慕容永聞其名，迎為謀主。

translations.literal: Later Murong Yong heard of his fame and welcomed him as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Later Murong Yong heard of his reputation and welcomed him as his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 先勸永據長子城，永遂稱制，以先為黃門郎、祕書監。

translations.literal: Xian urged Yong to hold Changzi city; Yong then assumed independent rule and appointed Xian as Gentleman-in-Attendance of the Yellow Gate and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xian urged Yong to hold Changzi city; Yong then assumed independent rule and appointed Xian Gentleman-in-Attendance of the Yellow Gate and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 垂滅永，徙於中山。

translations.literal: When Chui destroyed Yong, Xian was moved to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui destroyed Yong, Xian was relocated to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，先於井陘歸順。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi, Xian submitted in allegiance at Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Huangshi era, Xian submitted to the Wei at Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 太祖問先曰：「卿何國人？

translations.literal: The Taizu asked Xian: "Of what state are you a subject?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu asked Xian, "Where do you come from?

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「臣本趙郡平棘人。

translations.literal: Xian said: "This subject is originally a man of Pingji in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "I am originally from Pingji in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「朕聞中山土廣民殷，信爾以不？

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "We have heard that Zhongshan is broad in land and abundant in people—is this true?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said, "I have heard that Zhongshan is broad in territory and rich in population—is that true?

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「臣少官長安，仍事長子，後乃還鄉，觀望民士，實自殷廣。

translations.literal: Xian said: "This subject in youth served at Chang'an, then served at Changzi, and later returned home; observing the people and gentry, it is indeed abundant and broad.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "In my youth I served at Chang'an, then at Changzi, and later returned home; from what I observed of the people and the gentry, the region is indeed rich and populous.

sentences.zh: 」又問先曰：「朕聞長子中有李先者，卿其是乎？

translations.literal: He again asked Xian: "We have heard that among those at Changzi there is one Li Xian—are you that person?
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "I have heard there is a Li Xian at Changzi—are you he?

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「小臣是也。

translations.literal: Xian said: "This minor official is he.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "I am he.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「卿識朕不？

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "Do you recognize Us?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu asked, "Do you recognize me?

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「陛下聖德膺符，澤被八表，龍顏挺特，臣安敢不識。

translations.literal: Xian said: "Your Majesty's sacred virtue has received the Mandate, your beneficence reaches the eight directions, your dragon countenance is outstanding—how could this subject dare not recognize you?
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "Your Majesty's sacred virtue has received the Mandate, your beneficence reaches to every quarter, your august countenance is unmistakable—how could I fail to recognize you?

sentences.zh: 」太祖又問曰：「卿祖父及身官悉歷何官？

translations.literal: The Taizu again asked: "What offices did your grandfather and you yourself hold?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu asked further, "What offices did your grandfather and you yourself hold?

sentences.zh: 」先對曰：「臣大父重，晉平陽太守、大將軍右司馬。

translations.literal: Xian replied: "This subject's great-grandfather Chong was Jin Governor of Pingyang and Right Marshal under the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "My great-grandfather Chong was governor of Pingyang under the Jin and Right Marshal under the Grand General.

sentences.zh: 父樊，石虎樂安太守、左中郎將。

translations.literal: His father Fan was Shi Hu's Governor of Le'an and General of the Left Gentlemen of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fan had served Shi Hu as governor of Le'an and as General of the Left Gentlemen of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 臣，苻丕尚書右主客郎，慕容永祕書監、高密侯。

translations.literal: This subject was Fu Pi's Right Master of Guests in the Masters of Writing, and Murong Yong's Director of the Secretariat and Marquis of Gaomi.
translations.idiomatic: I served Fu Pi as Right Master of Guests in the Masters of Writing, and Murong Yong as Director of the Secretariat and Marquis of Gaomi.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「卿既宿士，屢歷名官，經學所通，何典為長？

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "You are a veteran scholar who has repeatedly held distinguished offices—in the classics you have mastered, which do you excel at?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said, "You are a seasoned scholar who has repeatedly held distinguished offices—which of the classics do you know best?

sentences.zh: 」先對曰：「臣才識愚闇，少習經史，年荒廢忘，十猶通六。

translations.literal: Xian replied: "This subject's talent and knowledge are dull and obscure; in youth I studied the classics and histories, but with years they have fallen into neglect and I forget—of ten I may still retain six.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "My talent is dull; I studied the classics and histories in youth, but with age much has slipped away—I might retain six parts in ten.

sentences.zh: 」又問：「兵法風角，卿悉通不？

translations.literal: He again asked: "Military treatises and wind-direction divination—do you fully understand them?
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "Military treatises and wind-direction divination—do you understand them fully?

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「亦曾習讀，不能明解。

translations.literal: Xian said: "I have also studied them, but cannot grasp them clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "I have studied them, but cannot claim to understand them well.

sentences.zh: 」太祖曰：「慕容永時，卿用兵不？

translations.literal: The Taizu said: "Under Murong Yong, did you command troops?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu asked, "Under Murong Yong, did you take part in military affairs?

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「臣時蒙顯任，實參兵事。」

translations.literal: Xian said: "At that time this subject received a prominent appointment and truly participated in military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "At that time I held a prominent appointment and was indeed involved in military affairs."

sentences.zh: 太祖後以先為丞相衞王府左長史。

translations.literal: The Taizu later appointed Xian Left Chief Clerk in the household of Prince Wei, Guardian of the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu later appointed Xian left chief clerk in the household of Prince Wei, Guardian of the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 從儀平鄴，到義臺，破慕容驎軍，回定中山，先每一進策，所向克平。

translations.literal: Following the campaign that pacified Ye, arriving at Yitai, defeating Murong Lin's army, and returning to secure Zhongshan—each time Xian offered counsel, wherever they went they achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign that pacified Ye, at Yitai, in the defeat of Murong Lin's army, and in the return to secure Zhongshan—whenever Xian offered counsel, success followed.

sentences.zh: 車駕還代，以先為尚書右中兵郎。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Dai, Xian was appointed Right Central Troops Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Dai, Xian was appointed Right Central Troops Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂先曰：「今蠕蠕屢來犯塞，朕欲討之，卿以為何如？

translations.literal: The Taizu said to Xian: "Now the Rouran repeatedly come raiding the frontier; We wish to campaign against them—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu said to Xian, "The Rouran have been raiding the frontier again and again; I wish to campaign against them—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」先曰：「蠕蠕不識天命，竄伏荒朔，屢來偷竊，驚動邊民。

translations.literal: Xian said: "The Rouran do not recognize Heaven's Mandate; they hide in the wild northern wastes and repeatedly come stealing, alarming the frontier people.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said, "The Rouran do not recognize Heaven's Mandate; they skulk in the northern wilderness and raid again and again, terrorizing the frontier population.

sentences.zh: 陛下神武，威德遐振，舉兵征之，必將摧殄。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is divinely martial; your authority and virtue resound far—if you raise troops to campaign against them, you will surely crush and destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is divinely martial, your authority and virtue resound far and wide—raise troops against them and you will surely destroy them.

sentences.zh: 」車駕於是北伐，大破蠕蠕。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage thereupon marched north and inflicted a great defeat on the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon marched north and inflicted a crushing defeat on the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 賞先奴婢三口，馬牛羊五十頭。

translations.literal: Xian was rewarded with three male and female slaves, and fifty head of horses, cattle, and sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was rewarded with three slaves and fifty head of horses, cattle, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 轉七兵郎，遷博士、定州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Seventh Troops Gentleman, then promoted to Erudite and Chief Rectifier of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Seventh Troops Gentleman and promoted to erudite and Chief Rectifier of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖問先曰：「天下何書最善，[10]可以益人神智？

translations.literal: The Taizu asked Xian: "What book under Heaven is the best [10] for enriching human intelligence?
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu asked Xian, "What book in all the world is best [10] for enriching the mind and spirit?

sentences.zh: 」先對曰：「唯有經書。

translations.literal: Xian replied: "Only the canonical scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "Only the canonical scriptures.

sentences.zh: 三皇五帝治化之典，可以補王者神智。

translations.literal: The classics of governance and transformation by the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors can supplement a king's intelligence and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The classics of governance by the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors can sharpen a ruler's mind and spirit.

sentences.zh: 」又問曰：「天下書籍，凡有幾何？

translations.literal: He again asked: "Books under Heaven—altogether how many are there?
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "How many books exist in all the world?

sentences.zh: 朕欲集之，如何可備？

translations.literal: We wish to collect them—how can they be assembled?
translations.idiomatic: I wish to collect them—how might that be accomplished?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「伏羲創制，帝王相承，以至於今，世傳國記，天文祕緯不可計數。

translations.literal: He replied: "From Fuxi's creation, emperors and kings succeeded one another down to today; dynastic records handed down through generations, astronomical secrets and apocryphal weft-texts—beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "From Fuxi's creations down through successive dynasties to the present, the records transmitted from age to age, the astronomical texts and apocryphal writings—they are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠欲集之，嚴制天下諸州郡縣搜索備送，主之所好，集亦不難。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to collect them, strictly order all prefectures, commanderies, and counties under Heaven to search and deliver them in full—what the lord desires to collect is not hard to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to collect them, issue strict orders to every province, commandery, and county to search and deliver books—what the sovereign desires is not hard to gather.

sentences.zh: 」太祖於是班制天下，經籍稍集。

translations.literal: The Taizu thereupon issued orders throughout the realm, and the canonical texts were gradually assembled.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu thereupon issued orders throughout the realm, and the canonical texts were gradually brought together.

sentences.zh: 太祖之討姚興於柴壁也，問先曰：「興屯天渡，平據柴壁，相為表裏。

translations.literal: When the Taizu was campaigning against Yao Xing at Chaibi, he asked Xian: "Xing is encamped at Tiandu and Ping holds Chaibi—they support each other inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu was campaigning against Yao Xing at Chaibi, he asked Xian, "Yao Xing is encamped at Tiandu and Ping holds Chaibi—they are mutually supporting positions.

sentences.zh: 今欲殄之，計將安出？

translations.literal: Now We wish to exterminate them—what plan should be devised?
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to destroy them—what plan do you propose?

sentences.zh: 」先對曰：「臣聞兵以正合，戰以奇勝。

translations.literal: Xian replied: "This subject has heard that in war one engages with the orthodox formation and wins by the unorthodox strike.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "I have heard that in war one engages with orthodox force and wins through unorthodox maneuvers.

sentences.zh: 如聞姚興欲屯兵天渡，利其糧道。

translations.literal: As I hear, Yao Xing wishes to encamp troops at Tiandu to profit from the grain supply route.
translations.idiomatic: As I understand, Yao Xing intends to encamp at Tiandu to control the grain supply route.

sentences.zh: 及其未到之前，遣奇兵先邀天渡，柴壁左右，嚴設伏兵，備其表裏。

translations.literal: Before he arrives, dispatch unorthodox troops first to intercept at Tiandu, and on both sides of Chaibi strictly deploy hidden troops to guard against inside and outside support.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrives, send a strike force to intercept at Tiandu, and on both flanks of Chaibi deploy ambush troops to block mutual reinforcement.

sentences.zh: 以陛下神策，觀時而動，興欲進不得，退又乏糧。

translations.literal: With Your Majesty's divine strategy, watching the moment and acting—Xing wishing to advance cannot, and if he retreats he lacks grain.
translations.idiomatic: With Your Majesty's divine strategy, acting when the moment is right—Yao Xing will be unable to advance, and if he retreats he will lack supplies.

sentences.zh: [11]夫高者為敵所棲，深者為敵所囚，兵法所忌而興居之，可不戰而取。

translations.literal: [11] One who occupies the heights is where the enemy will perch; one who dwells deep is where the enemy will imprison—what military treatises forbid is precisely where Xing has placed himself; he can be taken without battle.
translations.idiomatic: [11] High ground invites the enemy to settle on you; deep positions invite encirclement—the very mistakes military treatises warn against are the positions Yao Xing has taken; he can be captured without a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 」太祖從其計，興果敗歸。

translations.literal: The Taizu followed his plan, and Xing indeed suffered defeat and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu followed his plan, and Yao Xing was indeed defeated and forced to retreat.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，問左右舊臣之中為先帝所親信者有誰。

translations.literal: When the Mingyuan came to the throne, he asked who among the old ministers had been most trusted by the Former Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan came to the throne, he asked which of the veteran officials had been most trusted by his predecessor.

sentences.zh: 時新息公王洛兒對曰：「有李先者，最為先帝所知。

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Xixin Wang Luo'er replied: "There is Li Xian, whom the Former Emperor knew best.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Duke of Xixin Wang Luo'er replied, "Li Xian was the man the Former Emperor knew and trusted best.

sentences.zh: 」太宗召先引見，問曰：「卿有何功行，而蒙先帝所識？

translations.literal: The Mingyuan summoned Xian for audience and asked: "What achievements and conduct have you, that you earned recognition from the Former Emperor?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan summoned Xian for an audience and asked, "What merit or virtue earned you the Former Emperor's favor?

sentences.zh: 」先對曰：「臣愚細，才行無聞，適以忠直奉上，更無異能。

translations.literal: Xian replied: "This subject is coarse and dull; talent and conduct are without reputation—I merely served with loyalty and uprightness, with no other special ability.
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "I am coarse and undistinguished; my talent and conduct are nothing special—I merely served faithfully and uprightly, with no other gift.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「卿試言舊事。

translations.literal: The Mingyuan said: "Try telling Us of old affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan said, "Tell me something of the old days.

sentences.zh: 」先對曰：「臣聞堯舜之教，化民如子；

translations.literal: Xian replied: "This subject has heard that in the teaching of Yao and Shun, they transformed the people as sons;
translations.idiomatic: Xian replied, "I have heard that Yao and Shun governed by treating the people as their own children;

sentences.zh: 三王任賢，天下懷服。

translations.literal: the Three Kings employed the worthy, and all under Heaven submitted in their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: the Three Kings employed the worthy, and the realm submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 今陛下躬秉勞謙，六合歸德，士女能言，莫不慶抃。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty personally upholds diligent humility; the six directions return to your virtue—men and women who can speak, none fail to celebrate and clap.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty personally upholds diligence and humility, and the whole realm returns to your virtue—every man and woman who can speak celebrates with joy.

sentences.zh: 」俄而召先讀韓子連珠二十二篇、太公兵法十一事。

translations.literal: Presently he summoned Xian to read twenty-two chapters of Han Feizi's Linked Pearls and eleven items from Taigong's Military Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Presently he had Xian recite twenty-two chapters of Han Feizi's Linked Pearls and eleven passages from Taigong's Military Treatise.

sentences.zh: 詔有司曰：「先所知者，皆軍國大事，自今常宿於內。

translations.literal: An edict to the responsible offices stated: "What Xian knows concerns great affairs of army and state; from now on he shall regularly lodge within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: An edict to the relevant offices stated, "Xian's knowledge bears on great military and state affairs; from now on he is to lodge regularly within the palace.

sentences.zh: 」賜先絹五十匹、絲五十斤、雜綵五十匹。

translations.literal: Xian was granted fifty bolts of silk, fifty jin of raw silk, and fifty bolts of mixed-colored silk.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was granted fifty bolts of silk, fifty jin of raw silk, and fifty bolts of mixed-colored silk.

sentences.zh: 御馬一匹。

translations.literal: One imperial horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given one imperial horse.

sentences.zh: 拜安東將軍、壽春侯，賜隸戶二十二。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Shouchun, and granted twenty-two dependent households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Marquis of Shouchun, and granted twenty-two dependent households.

sentences.zh: 詔先與上黨王長孫道生率師襲馮跋乙連城，克之，悉虜其眾。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xian and Prince of Shangdang Changsun Daosheng to lead troops in a surprise attack on Feng Ba's Yilian city; they captured it and took all its people captive.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Xian and Prince of Shangdang Changsun Daosheng to lead troops in a surprise attack on Feng Ba's city of Yilian; they captured it and took all its defenders captive.

sentences.zh: 乃進討和龍。

translations.literal: They then advanced to attack Helong.
translations.idiomatic: They then advanced to attack Helong.

sentences.zh: 先言於道生曰：「宜密使兵人人備青草一束，各五尺圍，用填城塹。

translations.literal: Xian said to Daosheng: "You should secretly have every soldier prepare a bundle of green grass, each five chi in circumference, to fill the moat.
translations.idiomatic: Xian said to Daosheng, "You should secretly order every soldier to prepare a bundle of green grass, each five chi around, to fill the moat.

sentences.zh: 攻其西南，絕其外援，勒兵急攻，賊必可擒。

translations.literal: Attack from the southwest, cut off their external aid, urge the troops to press the attack—the bandits can surely be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Strike from the southwest, cut off their outside support, and press the attack hard—the enemy can surely be taken.

sentences.zh: 」道生不從，遂掠民而還。

translations.literal: Daosheng did not follow this, but plundered the people and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Daosheng did not follow his advice, plundered the populace, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後出為武邑太守，有治名。

translations.literal: Later he was sent out as Governor of Wuyi and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was later sent out as governor of Wuyi and earned a reputation for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，徵為內都大官。

translations.literal: When the Shizu came to the throne, he was summoned as Grand Officer of the Inner Court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu came to the throne, he was recalled to serve as Grand Officer of the Inner Court.

sentences.zh: 神䴥二年卒，年九十五。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenju he died, aged ninety-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of the Shenju era, aged ninety-five.

sentences.zh: 詔賜金縷命服一襲，贈定州刺史、中山公，諡曰文懿。

translations.literal: An edict granted one suit of gold-thread court robes for the living; he was posthumously granted the titles Governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Zhongshan, with the posthumous name Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him one suit of gold-thread court robes; he was posthumously made governor of Dingzhou and Duke of Zhongshan, with the posthumous name Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 子冏，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Jiong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiong succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 為京兆、濟陰二郡太守。

translations.literal: He served as Governor of the two commanderies of Jingzhao and Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He served as governor of Jingzhao and Jiyin commanderies.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子鍾葵，襲爵，降為子。

translations.literal: His son Zhongkui inherited the title, which was reduced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongkui succeeded to the title, which was reduced to the rank of viscount.

sentences.zh: 鍾葵弟鳳子，鳳子弟虬子，並中書博士。

translations.literal: Zhongkui's younger brother Fengzi, and Fengzi's younger brother Qiuzi, were both Erudites of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongkui's younger brother Fengzi and Fengzi's younger brother Qiuzi both served as erudites in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 鳳子子預，字元愷。

translations.literal: Fengzi's son Yu, style name Yuankai.
translations.idiomatic: Fengzi's son Yu had the style name Yuankai.

sentences.zh: 少為中書學生。

translations.literal: In youth he was a student of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was a student in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 聰敏強識，涉獵經史。

translations.literal: Quick and keen in memory, he ranged widely through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted with a powerful memory, he ranged widely through the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 太和初，歷祕書令、齊郡王友。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe he successively served as Chief of the Secretariat and Companion to the Prince of Qijun.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taihe era he served successively as Chief of the Secretariat and companion to the Prince of Qijun.

sentences.zh: 出為征西大將軍長史，帶馮翊太守。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Chief Clerk to the General Who Campaigns West and concurrently served as Governor of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as chief clerk to the General Who Campaigns West, concurrently serving as governor of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 積數年，府解罷郡，遂居長安。

translations.literal: After several years the headquarters was dissolved and his governorship ended; he then resided at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After several years the headquarters was dissolved and his concurrent governorship ended; he settled in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 每羨古人餐玉之法，乃採訪藍田，躬往攻掘。

translations.literal: He always admired the ancient method of dining on jade; he therefore inquired about Lantian and went in person to dig and excavate.
translations.idiomatic: He long admired the ancient practice of consuming jade; he traveled to Lantian and dug there himself.

sentences.zh: 得若環璧雜器形者大小百餘，稍得粗黑者，亦篋盛以還，而至家觀之，皆光潤可玩。

translations.literal: He obtained over a hundred pieces large and small in the shapes of rings, bi disks, and miscellaneous vessels; some that seemed coarse and dark he also packed in cases and brought back, but when he viewed them at home, all were lustrous and pleasing to handle.
translations.idiomatic: He found more than a hundred pieces in the shapes of rings, bi disks, and assorted vessels; even pieces that seemed coarse and dark in the field he packed up and brought home—and once home, all proved lustrous and lovely.

sentences.zh: 預乃椎七十枚為屑，日服食之，餘多惠人。

translations.literal: Yu then ground seventy pieces to powder, took them daily as food, and gave the remainder generously to others.
translations.idiomatic: Yu ground seventy pieces into powder, consumed a daily dose, and gave much of the rest away to others.

sentences.zh: 後預及聞者更求於故處，皆無所見。

translations.literal: Later Yu and those who heard of it searched again at the former spot and found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yu and others who heard of it searched the same spot again and found nothing.

sentences.zh: 馮翊公源懷等得其玉，琢為器佩，皆鮮明可寶。

translations.literal: Duke of Fengyi Yuan Huai and others obtained his jade, carved it into vessels and ornaments, all bright and worthy as treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Fengyi Yuan Huai and others obtained some of his jade, carved it into vessels and ornaments, all bright and precious.

sentences.zh: 預服經年，云有效驗，而世事寢食不禁節，又加之好酒損志，及疾篤，謂妻子曰：「服玉屏居山林，排棄嗜欲，或當大有神力，而吾酒色不絕，自致於死，非藥過也。

translations.literal: Yu consumed it for more than a year and said there was proof of efficacy, yet in worldly affairs he did not restrain eating and sleeping, and moreover his fondness for wine harmed his resolve; when gravely ill he told his wife and children: "Taking jade while dwelling in seclusion in mountains and forests, casting off desires—one might attain great divine power; but I never ceased wine and women and brought death upon myself—it is not the medicine's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yu consumed jade for more than a year and claimed it worked, yet he indulged freely in food and sleep and his love of wine dulled his resolve; when his illness grew grave he told his wife and children, "Taking jade in mountain seclusion, renouncing desire—one might gain great spiritual power; but I never gave up wine and women and brought this on myself—the jade is not to blame.

sentences.zh: 然吾尸體必當有異，勿便速殯，令後人知餐服之妙。

translations.literal: Yet my corpse will surely show something unusual—do not hasten the encoffining; let later people know the wonder of dining on jade.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my body will surely show something unusual—do not hasten to bury me; let later generations know the wonder of consuming jade."

sentences.zh: 」時七月中旬，長安毒熱，預停尸四宿，而體色不變。

translations.literal: It was mid-seventh month; Chang'an was blisteringly hot; Yu's corpse lay four nights and his bodily color did not change.
translations.idiomatic: It was mid-July; Chang'an was sweltering; Yu's corpse lay unburied for four nights, yet his complexion did not change.

sentences.zh: 其妻常氏以玉珠二枚唅之，口閉。

translations.literal: His wife the Lady Chang placed two jade pearls in his mouth to hold them, but his mouth was closed.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Chang tried to place two jade pearls in his mouth, but his mouth was closed.

sentences.zh: 常謂之曰：「君自云餐玉有神驗，何故不受唅也？

translations.literal: Lady Chang said to him: "You yourself said dining on jade had divine efficacy—why will you not accept the mouth-pearl?
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chang said to him, "You yourself said consuming jade had miraculous effects—why won't you take the mouth-pearls?

sentences.zh: 」言訖齒啟，納珠，因噓屬其口，都無穢氣。

translations.literal: When she had finished speaking, his teeth opened; she inserted the pearls, and as she breathed into his mouth there was no foul odor at all.
translations.idiomatic: As she finished speaking, his teeth parted; she placed the pearls in his mouth, breathed into it, and there was no foul odor whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 舉斂於棺，堅直不傾委。

translations.literal: When he was placed in the coffin for encoffining, he remained rigid and straight without slumping.
translations.idiomatic: When he was placed in the coffin, his body remained rigid and straight without slumping.

sentences.zh: 死時猶有遺玉屑數斗，[12]橐盛納諸棺中。

translations.literal: At death he still had several dou of leftover jade powder; [12] it was bagged and placed in the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he still had several dou of leftover jade powder; [12] it was bagged and placed in the coffin with him.

sentences.zh: 初天興中，先子密問於先曰：「子孫永為魏臣，將復事他主也？

translations.literal: Early in the Tianxing era, Xian's son secretly asked Xian: "Will our descendants forever serve Wei as subjects, or will they serve another lord again?
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianxing era, Xian's son quietly asked him, "Will our descendants always serve Wei, or will they serve another master?

sentences.zh: 」先告曰：「未也。

translations.literal: Xian told him: "Not yet.
translations.idiomatic: Xian told him, "Not yet.

sentences.zh: 國家政化長遠，不可卒窮。

translations.literal: The state's governance and transformation extend far; they cannot soon be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The state's governance and civilizing influence extend far into the future; they cannot soon come to an end.

sentences.zh: 」自皇始至齊受禪，實百五十餘歲矣。

translations.literal: From Huangshi to Qi's reception of the Mandate was in fact more than one hundred fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huangshi era to Qi's reception of the Mandate was in fact more than a hundred and fifty years.

sentences.zh: 賈彝，字彥倫，本武威姑臧人也。

translations.literal: Jia Yi, style name Yanlun, was originally a man of Gugang in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi, whose style name was Yanlun, was originally from Gugang in Wuwei commandery.

sentences.zh: 六世祖敷，魏幽州刺史、廣川都亭侯，子孫因家焉。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Fu was Wei Governor of Youzhou and Marquis of Duting of Guangchuan; his descendants therefore made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Fu had served as governor of Youzhou under Wei and as Marquis of Duting of Guangchuan; the family settled there.

sentences.zh: 父為苻堅鉅鹿太守，坐訕謗繫獄。

translations.literal: His father served Fu Jian as Governor of Julu and was imprisoned for slander.
translations.idiomatic: His father had served Fu Jian as governor of Julu and was imprisoned on a charge of slander.

sentences.zh: 彝年十歲，詣長安訟父獲申，遠近歎之，僉曰：「此子英俊，賈誼之後，莫之與京。

translations.literal: Yi at age ten went to Chang'an to plead his father's case and won its vindication; near and far sighed in admiration, all saying: "This child is outstanding—after Jia Yi, none can match him.
translations.idiomatic: At ten Yi went to Chang'an to plead his father's case and won his release; people far and near marveled, saying, "This boy is brilliant—since Jia Yi, none can match him.

sentences.zh: 」弱冠，為慕容垂驃騎大將軍、遼西王農記室參軍。

translations.literal: At weak cap he served Murong Chui as Adjunct in the Secretariat to the Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Prince of Liaoxi Nong.
translations.idiomatic: In early manhood he served Murong Chui as secretariat adjutant to the Rapid Cavalry Grand General, Prince of Liaoxi Nong.

sentences.zh: 太祖先聞其名，嘗遣使者求彝於垂。

translations.literal: The Taizu had earlier heard his name and once sent an envoy to request Yi from Chui.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu had already heard of him and once sent an envoy to request Yi from Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 垂彌增器敬，更加寵秩，遷驃騎長史，帶昌黎太守。

translations.literal: Chui only increased his respect and regard, further enhancing his rank and favor, promoting him to Chief Clerk of the Rapid Cavalry and concurrently appointing him Governor of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui only increased his esteem, further promoted and favored him, making him chief clerk of the Rapid Cavalry headquarters and concurrently governor of Changli.

sentences.zh: 垂遣其太子寶來寇，大敗於參合陂，執彝及其從兄代郡太守潤等。

translations.literal: Chui sent his heir Bao to raid; at Canhepo they suffered a great defeat, and Yi together with his elder cousin Run, Governor of Da commandery, and others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui sent his heir Bao on a raid; at Canhepo they were routed, and Yi was captured together with his elder cousin Run, governor of Da commandery, and others.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，拜尚書左丞，參預國政，加給事中。

translations.literal: When the Taizu took the throne, Yi was appointed Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, participated in state affairs, and was given the additional title Attendant Within the Gates.
translations.idiomatic: When the Taizu took the throne, Yi was made Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, took part in state affairs, and was given the added title Attendant Within the Gates.

sentences.zh: 於鄴置行臺，與尚書和跋鎮鄴，招攜初附。

translations.literal: A mobile headquarters was set up at Ye; together with He Ba, Minister of the Masters of Writing, Yi garrisoned Ye and won over those newly submitting.
translations.idiomatic: A mobile headquarters was established at Ye; together with Minister of the Masters of Writing He Ba, Yi garrisoned Ye and won over newly submitted populations.

sentences.zh: 久乃召還。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 天賜末，彝請詣溫湯療病，為叛胡所拘執，送於姚興，積數年，遁歸。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianci, Yi requested to go to hot springs to treat an illness; he was seized by rebel Hu and delivered to Yao Xing; after several years he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Tianci era Yi asked to visit hot springs to treat an illness; rebel Hu seized him and sent him to Yao Xing; after several years he escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 又為屈丐所執，與語悅之，拜祕書監。

translations.literal: He was again seized by Juqu, who was pleased in conversation with him and appointed him Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was seized again by Juqu, who took a liking to him in conversation and appointed him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 年六十一，卒。

translations.literal: At age sixty-one he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 世祖平赫連昌，子秀迎其尸柩，葬于代南。

translations.literal: When the Shizu pacified Helian Chang, his son Xiu received the coffin and buried him south of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu pacified Helian Chang, his son Xiu received the coffin and buried him south of Dai.

sentences.zh: 秀，歷中書博士，遷中書侍郎、太子中庶子、揚烈將軍，賜爵陽都男，本州大中正。

translations.literal: Xiu successively served as Erudite of the Secretariat, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household, General Who Inspires Awe, was enfeoffed as Baron of Yangdu, and was Chief Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu served successively as erudite in the Secretariat, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, vice director in the crown prince's household, and General Who Inspires Awe; he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yangdu and made Chief Rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 恭宗崩，以爵還第。

translations.literal: When the Gongzong died, he returned his title and went home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gongzong died, he surrendered his title and retired.

sentences.zh: 既而掌吏曹事。

translations.literal: Thereafter he took charge of personnel affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He then took charge of personnel affairs.

sentences.zh: 高宗以秀東宮舊臣，進爵陽都子，加振威將軍。

translations.literal: The Gaozong, because Xiu was an old minister of the Eastern Palace, advanced his title to Viscount of Yangdu and gave him the additional title General Who Shakes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xiu had been an old minister of the Eastern Palace, the Gaozong raised his title to Viscount of Yangdu and gave him the added title General Who Shakes Might.

sentences.zh: [13]時丞相乙渾擅作威福，多所殺害。

translations.literal: At that time Chancellor Yi Hun arrogated authority and prestige, killing many people. [13]
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chancellor Yi Hun arrogated power and prestige and killed many people. [13]

sentences.zh: 渾妻庶姓而求公主之號，屢言於秀，秀默然。

translations.literal: Hun's wife was of common surname yet sought the title of princess; she repeatedly spoke of this to Xiu, and Xiu remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's wife was of common birth yet sought the title of princess; she repeatedly raised the matter with Xiu, and Xiu said nothing.

sentences.zh: 渾曰：「公事無所不從，我請公主，不應何意？

translations.literal: Hun said: "In public affairs you refuse nothing—when I ask for the title of princess, what is the meaning of your refusal?
translations.idiomatic: Hun said, "You refuse me nothing in public affairs—when I ask for the title of princess for my wife, why do you refuse?

sentences.zh: 」秀慷慨大言，對曰：「公主之稱，王姬之號，尊寵之極，非庶族所宜。

translations.literal: Xiu spoke boldly and at length, replying: "The title of princess, the designation of a king's daughter, is the utmost in honor and favor—it is not fitting for a common clan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu answered boldly, "The title of princess, the designation of a king's daughter, is the highest honor—it is not fitting for a common clan.

sentences.zh: 若假竊此號，當必自咎。

translations.literal: If you falsely usurp this title, you will surely bring blame upon yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If you usurp that title falsely, you will surely bring ruin upon yourself.

sentences.zh: 秀寧死於今朝，不取笑於後日。

translations.literal: Xiu would rather die this morning than be mocked on a later day.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu would rather die today than be mocked tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」渾左右莫不失色，為之震懼，而秀神色自若。

translations.literal: Those at Hun's side all lost color and trembled in fear for him, yet Xiu's expression remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Those around Hun turned pale and trembled for him, yet Xiu's expression never changed.

sentences.zh: 渾夫妻默然含忿。

translations.literal: Hun and his wife silently harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Hun and his wife silently nursed their resentment.

sentences.zh: 他日，乃書太醫給事楊惠富臂作「老奴官慳」字，令以示秀。

translations.literal: On another day he wrote on the arm of Attendant Physician Yang Huifu the characters "old slave official stingy" and had him show it to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: On another day he wrote on the arm of Attendant Physician Yang Huifu the words "stingy old slave official" and had him show it to Xiu.

sentences.zh: 渾每欲伺隙陷之，會渾伏誅，遂得免難。

translations.literal: Hun always wished to seize an opportunity to entrap him, but when Hun was executed for his crimes Xiu was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Hun always sought an opportunity to destroy him, but when Hun was executed Xiu was spared.

sentences.zh: 秀執正守志，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Xiu's uprightness in holding to his principles was all of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's integrity and steadfastness were all of this kind.

sentences.zh: 時秀與中書令勃海高允俱以儒舊見重於時，皆選擬方岳，以詢訪見留，各聽長子出為郡守。

translations.literal: At that time Xiu together with Secretariat Director Gao Yun of Bohai were both valued as Confucian veterans; both were selected for regional governorships, but on consultation they were retained, each permitted to send his eldest son out as a commandery governor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xiu and Secretariat Director Gao Yun of Bohai were both valued as veteran Confucian scholars; both were selected for regional governorships but were kept at court after consultation, each allowed to send his eldest son out to serve as a commandery governor.

sentences.zh: 秀辭曰：「爰自愚微，承乏累紀，少而受恩，老無成效，恐先草露，無報殊私。

translations.literal: Xiu declined, saying: "From my humble beginnings I have borne unworthy office for many reigns; favored in youth and without achievement in old age, I fear I shall die before the dew falls and cannot repay extraordinary kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu declined, saying, "From humble beginnings I have held office through many reigns; favored in youth yet without achievement in old age, I fear I shall die before I can repay your extraordinary kindness.

sentences.zh: 豈直無功之子，超齊先達。

translations.literal: How could an unmeritorious son leap ahead of earlier worthies?
translations.idiomatic: How could an unworthy son leap ahead of earlier worthies?

sentences.zh: 雖仰感聖慈，而俯深驚懼。

translations.literal: Though I am moved by the sacred kindness above, inwardly I am deeply alarmed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am grateful for your kindness, I am deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 乞收成命，以安微臣。

translations.literal: I beg you to withdraw the order and put this humble minister at ease.
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to withdraw the order and set my mind at ease.

sentences.zh: 」遂固讓不受。

translations.literal: He thereupon firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 自始及終，歷奉五帝，雖不至大官，常掌機要。

translations.literal: From beginning to end he served five emperors; though he never reached the highest offices, he always handled confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From beginning to end he served five emperors; though he never reached the highest offices, he always handled confidential affairs.

sentences.zh: 而廉清儉約，不營資產。

translations.literal: Yet he was incorruptible, frugal, and abstemious, and did not accumulate property.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was incorruptible, frugal, and abstemious, and accumulated no property.

sentences.zh: 年七十三，遇疾，給醫藥，賜几杖。

translations.literal: At age seventy-three he fell ill; medicine was provided and a armrest and staff were granted.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy-three he fell ill; the court provided medicine and granted him an armrest and staff.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷舉動及大事不決，每遣尚書、高平公李敷就第訪決。

translations.literal: Whenever court actions and great affairs were undecided, the court would send Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Fu, Duke of Gaoping, to his residence for consultation and decision.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever major court decisions were unresolved, the court sent Minister of the Masters of Writing Li Fu, Duke of Gaoping, to his home for consultation.

sentences.zh: 皇興三年卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangxing he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the Huangxing era.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、冀州刺史、武邑公，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former generalship, the title Governor of Jizhou, and Duke of Wuyi, with the posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former generalship, made governor of Jizhou and Duke of Wuyi, with the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 子儁，字異隣，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Jun, style name Yilin, inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun, whose style name was Yilin, succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 拜祕書中散、軍曹令。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supernumerary Attendant of the Secretariat and Director of the Military Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed supernumerary attendant of the Secretariat and director of the Military Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為顯武將軍、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as General of Manifest Might and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General of Manifest Might and governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 依例降爵為伯。

translations.literal: According to precedent his title was reduced and he became a baron.
translations.idiomatic: Following precedent, his title was reduced and he became a baron.

sentences.zh: 先是，上洛置荊州，後改為洛州，在重山中，民不知學。

translations.literal: Earlier Jingzhou had been established at Shangluo, then changed to Luozhou; it lay deep in the mountains, and the people knew nothing of learning.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou had earlier been established at Shangluo, then renamed Luozhou; it lay deep in the mountains, and the people had no schooling.

sentences.zh: 儁乃表置學官，選聰悟者以教之。

translations.literal: Jun thereupon memorialized to establish school officials and select the quick-witted to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized to establish school officials and select quick-witted students to teach the people.

sentences.zh: 在州五載，清靖寡事，吏民亦安。

translations.literal: During five years in the province he was pure, tranquil, and seldom troubled by affairs; officials and commoners were also at peace.
translations.idiomatic: During five years in the province he governed with purity and tranquility; officials and commoners alike were at peace.

sentences.zh: 遷洛後，儁朝京師，賞以素帛。

translations.literal: After the move to Luoyang, when Jun came to court he was rewarded with plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital moved to Luoyang, Jun came to court and was rewarded with plain silk.

sentences.zh: 景明初卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingming he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Jingming era.

sentences.zh: 贈本將軍、光州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former generalship and the title Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his former generalship and made governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子叔休，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Shuxiu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuxiu succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 除給事中。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Within the Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Within the Gates.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子興，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Xing inherited the title.
