translations.idiomatic: His son Xing succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 興弟賓，歷尚書郎，以清素稱。

translations.literal: Xing's younger brother Bin successively served as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and was known for purity and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Xing's younger brother Bin served as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and was known for purity and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 出為黎陽太守，卒官。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Liyang and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as governor of Liyang and died in office.

sentences.zh: 潤曾孫禎，字叔願。

translations.literal: Run's great-grandson Zhen, style name Shuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Run's great-grandson Zhen had the style name Shuyuan.

sentences.zh: 學涉經史，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: He studied broadly in the classics and histories, and in mourning for his parents was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He studied broadly in the classics and histories and was famed for filial piety in mourning his parents.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為中書博士，副中書侍郎高聰使於江左。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he served as Erudite of the Secretariat and accompanied Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Gao Cong as envoy to the lands south of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he served as erudite in the Secretariat and accompanied Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Gao Cong as envoy to the south.

sentences.zh: 還，以母老患，輒過家定省，坐免官。

translations.literal: On his return, because his mother was old and ill he went straight home to visit her and was dismissed from office for it.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, because his mother was old and ill he went home to visit her without permission and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，徵為京兆王愉郎中令，行洛陽令。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned as Director of Gentlemen under Prince of Jingzhao Yu and acted as Magistrate of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was summoned as director of gentlemen under Prince of Jingzhao Yu and served as acting magistrate of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 轉治書侍御史、國子博士，加威遠將軍，行魯陽太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Imperial Censor, Erudite of the Imperial University, given the additional title General Who Expands the Distant, and acted as Governor of Luyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant Imperial Censor and erudite of the Imperial University, given the added title General Who Expands the Distant, and served as acting governor of Luyang.

sentences.zh: 清素，善撫接，得百姓情。

translations.literal: Pure and simple, he was skilled in winning people's hearts; he gained the affection of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and upright, he was skilled at winning people over and gained the common people's affection.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司徒諮議參軍、通直散騎常侍，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Consulting Adjunct of the Minister of Works, Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, and given the additional title Champion General.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to consulting adjutant under the Minister of Works and Regular Attendant of the Secretariat, with the added title Champion General.

sentences.zh: 正光中卒。

translations.literal: In the Zhengguang era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Zhengguang era.

sentences.zh: 贈平北將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the titles General Who Pacifies the North and Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 子子儒，司空田曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Ziru served as Adjunct of the Field Bureau under the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziru served as an adjunct in the Field Bureau under the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 禎兄子景儁，亦以學識知名，奉朝請。

translations.literal: Zhen's elder brother's son Jingjun was also known for learning and knowledge and served as Court Gentleman for Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen's nephew Jingjun was also known for learning and served as Court Gentleman for Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 遷京兆王愉府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Outer Troops Adjunct in the household of Prince of Jingzhao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to outer-troop adjutant in the household of Prince of Jingzhao Yu.

sentences.zh: 愉起逆於冀州，將授其官，景儁不受，愉殺之。

translations.literal: When Yu raised rebellion in Jizhou and was about to grant him office, Jingjun refused, and Yu killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu rebelled in Jizhou and was about to grant him office, Jingjun refused, and Yu had him killed.

sentences.zh: 永平中，贈東清河太守，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era he was posthumously granted the title Governor of Eastern Qinghe and given the posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping era he was posthumously made governor of Eastern Qinghe with the posthumous name Zhen.

sentences.zh: 景儁弟景興。

translations.literal: Jingjun's younger brother Jingxing.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun's younger brother Jingxing.

sentences.zh: 清峻鯁正。

translations.literal: Pure, stern, and upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was pure, stern, and upright.

sentences.zh: 少為州主簿，遂栖遲不仕。

translations.literal: In youth he was chief clerk of the province, then lingered in retirement and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served as the provincial chief clerk, then lived in retirement and refused office.

sentences.zh: 後葛榮陷冀州，為榮所虜，稱疾不拜。

translations.literal: Later when Ge Rong seized Jizhou he was captured by Rong; he claimed illness and would not bow.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Ge Rong seized Jizhou, he was captured; he claimed illness and refused to bow.

sentences.zh: 景興每捫膝而言曰：「吾不負汝。

translations.literal: Jingxing would each time press his knees and say: "I do not fail you.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxing would press his knees and say each time, "I have not failed you.

sentences.zh: 」以不拜葛榮故也。

translations.literal: This was because he would not bow to Ge Rong.
translations.idiomatic: He said this because he had refused to bow to Ge Rong.

sentences.zh: 薛提，太原人也。

translations.literal: Xue Ti was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Ti came from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 皇始中，補太學生，拜侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Huangshi era he was appointed a student of the Imperial University and promoted to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huangshi era he entered the Imperial University and was appointed Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 累遷散騎常侍、太子太保，賜爵歷陽侯，加晉兵將軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Secretariat and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, enfeoffed as Marquis of Liyang, and given the additional title General of Jin Troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Secretariat and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, enfeoffed as Marquis of Liyang, and given the added title General of Jin Troops.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮東大將軍、冀州刺史，進爵太原公。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Grand General Who Guards the East and Governor of Jizhou, and advanced in title to Duke of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Grand General Who Guards the East and governor of Jizhou, and his title was advanced to Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 所在有聲績。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he had a reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he earned a reputation for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 徵為侍中，治都曹事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Attendant and took charge of Capital Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Attendant and took charge of Capital Bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: When the Shizu died, the death was kept secret and mourning was not announced.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu died, the death was kept secret and mourning was not announced.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射蘭延、侍中和匹等議，[14]以為皇孫幼冲，宜立長君，徵秦王翰置之祕室。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Lan Yan, Attendant He Pi, and others deliberated [14] that because the imperial grandson was young and tender, a mature ruler ought to be established; they summoned Prince of Qin Han and placed him in a secret chamber.

sentences.zh: 則進爵應該在濬即位後，不會在拓跋弘即位後追敍。

translations.literal: Then the advancement of title should have come after Jun took the throne, not as a retrospective account after Tuoba Hong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The advancement should therefore have occurred after Jun took the throne, not as a retrospective account after Tuoba Hong came to power.

sentences.zh: 知這裏「加振威將軍」下當有脫文，却非「高宗」字訛。

translations.literal: It is known that below "given the additional title General Who Shakes Might" there must be missing text, yet it is not an error for the character "Gaozong."
translations.idiomatic: It appears that text is missing after "given the added title General Who Shakes Might," but this is not simply an error for "Gaozong."

sentences.zh: 侍中和匹等議 北史卷二八薛提傳「匹」作「延」。

translations.literal: Attendant He Pi and others deliberated — History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 28, biography of Xue Ti, writes "延" for "匹."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Attendant He Pi and others deliberated": History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 28, biography of Xue Ti, reads "延" (Yan) for "匹" (Pi).

sentences.zh: 按卷九四宗愛傳作「和疋」，通鑑卷一二六

translations.literal: Note: juan 94, biography of Zong Ai, writes "He Pi"; Zizhi Tongjian, juan 126
translations.idiomatic: Note: juan 94, biography of Zong Ai, writes "He Pi"; Zizhi Tongjian, juan 126

sentences.zh: 〈三九七三頁〉

translations.literal: 〈Page 3973〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Page 3973〉

sentences.zh: 作「和𤴓」。

translations.literal: writes "He He" (variant form).
translations.idiomatic: reads "He He" (variant character).

sentences.zh: 疑本作「疋」，又寫作「𤴓」，即「雅」字，或讀作「匹」，故又寫作「匹」，訛作「延」。

translations.literal: It is suspected the original text read "Pi" (疋), also written with the variant character—that is, the character for "ya" (雅)—or read as "pi," hence also written as "pi," and then erroneously written as "yan."
translations.idiomatic: The original probably read "Pi" (疋), also written with a variant form of the character for "ya" (雅), or pronounced "pi" and written accordingly, then corrupted to "yan."

sentences.zh: 賈彝早播時學 北史卷二七傳論「學」作「譽」，是。

translations.literal: Jia Yi early spread his learning through the age — in the appraisal of the biography in History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 27, "learning" is written as "reputation"; this is correct.
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "Jia Yi early spread his learning through the age": in the appraisal in History of the Northern Dynasties, juan 27, "learning" (学) should read "reputation" (誉); that is correct.
